records.task: Generalised KG construction with a curriculum-tuned LLM: KG sub-tasks (sentence-level, few-shot, document-level and joint entity-relation extraction)
records.ss: some datasets are sampled from the originals for data balancing (Table 5, p. 10). consolidated row (four datasets with the same role).

records.use: Training and testing: EKG enhancement stage; OOD datasets used only for testing (GKG-LLM exceeds the second-best baseline on TCR and Causal-TB); stage-wise ablation (G-Micro, G-Mid).
records.dv: ACE2005, WIKIEVENTS, RAMS, MATRES, ESL, TB-Dense, Causal-TB, MAVEN-ERE, HiEve; held-out OOD test sets TCR (ETRE) and Causal-TB (ECRE)
records.task: Generalised KG construction: event KG sub-tasks (event detection, argument extraction, temporal, causal and subevent relation extraction)
records.ss: MAVEN-ERE subsets are sampled (Table 5, p. 10). consolidated row (event-level sub-tasks with the same role).

records.loc: Table 1, p. 5; Table 5, p. 10; Sec. 6, p. 11
records.use: Training and testing within the unified instruction-tuned framework.
records.dv: CoNLL (17,293 train / 3,454 test)
records.task: NER as a GKG sub-task
records.ri: the table groups NER near the commonsense-KG block; the paper only says CoNLL is used for training and testing NER (p. 11).

records.use: Dataset introduction: ontology (Tables 1-7), mapping of structured station data to triples, rule- and dictionary-based extraction from crawled text, entity alignment and storage in Neo4j.
records.dv: ISLKG (new; National Oceanographic Data Center of China observation-station data, crawled semi-structured and unstructured island pages compiled into an Island Text Corpus; 82,086 entities, 111 relationship types)
records.task: Island domain KG construction from multi-source data (ontology design; dictionary- and rule-based extraction; fusion; Neo4j storage)
records.dl: scarcity of island data makes the KG incomplete (Sec. 4.1, pp. 21-22).
records.ss: correctness of rule-based extraction depends on rule design, generalisability and the quality of the island text library, so extracted entities need quality evaluation (Sec. 3.1.4, p. 13). data available on request only (p. 25).

records.use: Dataset introduction: architecture and pipeline of a KG built from scratch; comparison of its motivation with Freebase, Wikidata, DBpedia, YAGO, ConceptNet and CN-DBpedia.
records.dv: Sogou knowledge graph (new; data from 136 websites such as Wikipedia and SogouBaike; 54 million entities and over 600 million entity links)
records.task: Industrial multi-source KG construction for web search (extraction, normalisation, merging, inference, storage)
records.ss: embedding-based inference (TransE, TransR) was judged not accurate enough for products (Sec. 3.4, p. 338).
records.ri: no quantitative evaluation of KG quality is reported.

records.loc: Sec. 3.1, Tables 1-2, pp. 8-11; Sec. 4, Table 3, Table 4, p. 15; Tables 5-6, pp. 16-17; Sec. 5, Figs. 9-10, pp. 19-21
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: NER and RE precision, recall and F1 vs CasRel, GPT-4 zero- and few-shot, REBEL and KnowGL (proposed NER F1 0.8875, RE F1 0.8948); ablations on continual learning and dynamic few-shot; extracted triples stored in Neo4j.
records.dv: Aerospace requirement dataset (new; 2,284 original requirement items from spacecraft system documents, augmented to 7,923 texts across telemetry, launch support, attitude control, ground command and propulsion; doccano annotation; 80:20 train/test)
records.task: Requirement-text KG construction with a domain-adapted LLM (GPT-4 augmentation with BERTScore filtering; LoRA continual learning of Qwen2.5-7B; dynamic few-shot CoT)
records.ss: aerospace requirement texts are scarce and often inaccessible (p. 2); data available on request only (p. 22).
records.ri: the 80:20 split is applied after GPT-4 augmentation, so the test set may contain generated texts derived from training items.

records.loc: Sec. 3.3, Table 1, pp. 4-5; Sec. 4.1, Table 2, Table 3, p. 6; Table 5, p. 7
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: Llama2-7B LoRA instruction tuning; NER compared with BERT-CRF, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (LLaMA-1600 precision 87.88%); effect of dataset quality (1,600 corrected vs 15,000 uncorrected) and epochs.
records.dv: LLM-TIKG instruction datasets (new; GPT-annotated and augmented, partly manually corrected: topic classification 2,000; entity and relation extraction 1,600 corrected / 15,000 uncorrected; TTP classification 38,946)
records.task: Threat-intelligence KG construction with a fine-tuned LLM (topic classification, entity and relation extraction, TTP extraction)
records.ss: the authors note a lack of authoritative open-source annotated threat-intelligence datasets (p. 1). recall is relatively low and hashes and similar entities are more likely to be omitted (p. 6).

records.use: Training and testing: accuracy, precision, recall and F1 of LLaMA-Tec and LLaMA-SubTec vs TTPDrill and Tram (LLaMA-Tec precision 96.53%).
records.dv: TTP dataset from MITRE ATT&CK malware examples and the Tram labelled dataset, augmented (229 techniques, 595 sub-techniques; 10:1 train/test; includes negative samples)
records.task: TTP classification of attack descriptions (MITRE ATT&CK techniques and sub-techniques)
records.ss: techniques not represented in the dataset are not treated as separate classes (p. 6).

records.loc: Sec. 5, Table 1, p. 48; Tables 2-5, pp. 49-53
records.use: Training and testing: improvement of several document-level RE models (CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, Context-aware and SOTA models) when injecting coreference and KG knowledge; analysis by mention count.
records.dv: DocRED (test labels not public) and DWIE (RE part; training set split 80/20 for validation), with Wikidata 2020-12-01 as the knowledge source
records.task: Document-level relation extraction with entity knowledge injection from a KG (KIRE)
records.dl: DocRED test labels are not public; DWIE has no validation set (p. 48).

records.loc: Abstract, p. 628; Secs. 3-5, pp. 631-640
records.use: Dataset introduction: ontology reuse, data integration, external links and reasoning rules described.
records.dv: IMGT-KG (new; integrated from IMGT immunogenetics databases; 79,670,110 triples, 10,430,268 entities, 673 concepts, 173 properties; SPARQL endpoint; Allen interval rules)
records.task: Domain KG construction for immunogenetics (IMGT-KG)
records.ri: resource paper; no task-level evaluation of the KG.

records.use: Testing: state-of-the-art supervised and few-shot RE systems (e.g., PFN, REBEL) evaluated on custom microbenchmark samples.
records.dv: RELD-RDF (six RE datasets in RDF: WebNLG, NYT-FB, Wikidata RE, Google-RE, DocRED, FewRel, SemEval2010); samples of 15 NYT-FB relations, 40 balanced FewRel-style relations and others
records.task: Benchmark sampling for relation extraction (REBench microbenchmarks)
records.ss: microbenchmarking is used to expose limitations of RE models and their components (p. 643).
records.ri: the paper lists the RELD-RDF members as six while naming seven datasets (p. 646).

records.loc: Sec. 3, p. 664; Sec. 5, Table 2, p. 672
records.use: Dataset introduction and application: pipeline outputs and statistics; visualisation tools for exploring topics and co-publications.
records.dv: ISSA Agritrop RDF dataset (new; CIRAD open archive articles with AGROVOC descriptors via Annif trained on about 12,000 articles; named entities linked to Wikidata, DBpedia and GeoNames; DOI-identified dump and SPARQL endpoint)
records.task: Pipeline for semantic indexing of a scientific archive (ISSA; Agritrop)
records.ss: URIs were not yet dereferenceable at the time of writing (p. 672).
records.dom: Scholarly and education; Cultural heritage and humanities; Food and agriculture

records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: precision, recall and F1 over 1,200 annotated statements; comparison with AI-KG.
records.dv: CS-KG (new; over 350M triples describing 41M statements from 6.7M Computer Science articles from MAG, about 10M entities, 179 relations); 1,200 manually annotated statements for evaluation
records.task: Large-scale automatic construction of a research KG of entities and claims (CS-KG)
records.dl: MAG was decommissioned in 2021; later versions will use OpenAlex (p. 681).
records.ss: produced fully automatically, so statements are not revised by humans (p. 692).

records.use: Dataset construction and application: transformation pipeline, provenance ontology (Table 1) and lessons learnt from the pilot.
records.dv: Public procurement open datasets from pilot partners (e.g., Portuguese JSON files) transformed with RML into KGs modelled with the eProcurement Ontology; transformation metadata modelled with DCAT-AP and PROV-O
records.task: Public procurement KG construction in a distributed data space (ePO, RML on the EU Big Data Test Infrastructure)
records.ss: limits in navigating JSON with RML prevented persistent URIs for lots; open data is often treated apart from internal data processes (pp. 765-766).

records.use: Training and testing: F1 for mention detection, typing, entity label, relation name and relation prediction vs generative IE baselines; user evaluation of recommendations with 30 users.
records.dv: Distantly supervised relation-extraction dataset extended with Wikidata annotations of triples found in Wikipedia abstracts; IBM Research internal KG linked to Wikidata
records.task: Corporate research KG induction (Wikidata Parser for generative information extraction)
records.ri: the internal KG and user study are not reproducible outside the organisation.
records.dom: Scholarly and education; Business, e-commerce and tourism

records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: EEL and RE evaluated on 100 randomly selected sentences (precision, recall, F1 by a human annotator); RDF statistics over all 12,015 sentences; precision of represented data judged by 4 student judges with Randolph's kappa; complete system vs baseline without NP-entity association.
records.dv: IT news corpus (new; 605 webpages from nine RSS providers such as BBC, DailyTech and Computer-Weekly; 12,015 sentences; 89,486 RDF statements generated)
records.task: KG construction from text via OpenIE, entity linking (Babelfy, DBpedia Spotlight, TagMe majority vote) and SRL, with n-ary RDF reification
records.ss: no gold-standard datasets exist for evaluating relations in the Semantic Web, so manual evaluation is used (Sec. 5.5, p. 352). English IT news only as a proof of concept; other domains left to future work (p. 349).
records.ri: kappa values are fair to moderate (Table 7, p. 353) and only four judges were used.

records.loc: Sec. 5.1, Fig. 5, p. 7; Sec. 5.2, Tables 1-4, Figs. 6-8, pp. 7-9; Sec. 5.3, Fig. 9, p. 9
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: held-out evaluation with PR curves, AUC and P@N vs PCNN-ONE, PCNN-BAGATT, PCNN-ATT-NIS and ablations (best AUC 0.491); predicted triples visualised in Neo4j (7 of 10 example predictions correct).
records.dv: Robotic fault diagnosis corpus (new; maintenance logs, books and articles; over 900 manually labelled sentences, over 17,000 unlabelled sentences; 11 relation categories; 5,860 event-argument entities and 5,205 semantic relationships)
records.task: Distant-supervision relation extraction for fault diagnosis KG construction (PCNN-ATTRA-RL)
records.ss: labelled data are limited and noisy sentences in the multi-source corpus are non-negligible (Sec. 6, p. 10). data available on request (p. 11).
records.ri: KG-level evaluation is a 10-triple illustration.

records.use: Dataset introduction: classification structure, attributes and relations defined, resources processed under text-representation norms and imported to build the ontology and KG.
records.dv: TCM KG (new; classification structure of 2,253 concepts covering diseases, symptoms, prescriptions, drugs, medical records, regions, doctors and dynasties; built from TCM vocabularies, encyclopedias and ancient books via a domain ontology construction platform)
records.task: Domain ontology and KG construction from ancient Chinese medicine texts
records.ri: no size of the instance KG and no evaluation are reported.

records.loc: Sec. III-B, p. 168090; Sec. III-E, Table 1, p. 168092; Tables 2-4, pp. 168093-168094
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: precision, recall and F1 of TextCNN vs three traditional classifiers and FastCNN.
records.dv: 3GPP RAN1 #98-Bis proposal dataset (new; 1,625 proposals in 12 subject categories; random 4:1 train/validation split)
records.task: Topic classification for information extraction from technical proposals (TextCNN)
records.ss: data are unevenly distributed, so documents that do not contribute to topic classification were filtered before selecting twelve categories (p. 168092).
records.ri: a single meeting's proposals; small for a CNN, as the authors note overfitting risk on small data (p. 168092).

records.use: Dataset introduction: data model, storage in Neo4j and query of proposal relations (e.g., revision chain of R1-1910434).
records.dv: 3GPP proposal KG (new; entity types TDoc, Member, Organization, Meeting, Category; relations such as revision between proposals)
records.task: Domain KG construction for technical documents (Neo4j)
records.ss: massive unstructured text still needs manual annotation and integration (Sec. V, p. 168097).
records.ri: KG size not reported.

records.loc: Sec. 3.1, pp. 3-4; Sec. 4.1, p. 8 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction: KG built with the platform's structured-data pipeline and stored in Neo4j.
records.dv: Medical KG crawled from jib.xywy.com (new; check items, department, disease, drug, food, producer, symptom; about 33,000 entities and 230,000 relations)
records.task: Semi-automated KG construction from structured data (platform data dictionary to Cypher)
records.ss: scalability to large-scale KGs and handling of noisy data are stated limitations (Sec. 5, PDF p. 13).
records.ri: no KG quality evaluation.
records.dom: Biomedical and health; Food and agriculture

records.loc: Sec. 4.2.3, Table 3, p. 9 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: MIE model vs Plain-Classifier and MIE-Classifier baselines from the dataset paper.
records.dv: Doctor-patient dialogue dataset of Zhang et al. (dialogues from medical websites, manually annotated labels)
records.task: KG construction from audio: medical information extraction (MIE) from doctor-patient dialogue
records.ri: split sizes are not reported in the PDF.

records.loc: Sec. 5.1, Table 3, p. 13; Tables 6-8, pp. 15-16; Figs. 11-12, pp. 13-14 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: precision, recall and F1 for entity recognition/classification and RE vs Bi-LSTM+CRF, BERT+Bi-LSTM+CRF, CMLA, IOG, LSTM+LSTM+Bias and EDAS; sentiment knowledge triples extracted for both domains.
records.dv: SemEval-2014 Task 4 restaurant (3,041 train / 800 test) and laptop (3,045 / 800) datasets, re-labelled with six sentiment categories and aspect types; restaurant training data augmented by comma-based scrambling
records.task: Sentiment KG construction: joint sentiment/aspect entity recognition (BBC-LSTM) and relation extraction (ED-Learning)
records.dl: attribute categories in the restaurant dataset are imbalanced (Sec. 5.1, p. 13).
records.ss: the model depends on the granularity of the dataset's emotion classification (six categories) (Sec. 8, p. 19). laptop aspect classifications are not given in advance, so they are excluded from comparison (p. 15).

records.use: Source dataset and analysis: KG generated from four web servers' logs; forensic use case queries (user activity) and per-source run-time of template extraction and graph building.
records.dv: AIT log dataset V1.1 (public; six days of testbed log data from multiple systems, 51.1 GB raw; Apache, audit, suricata, exim, auth, daemon, mail, syslog and user logs); 838.19 MB processed for the scenario into 84,827,361 triples (498.36 MB HDT)
records.task: Automated log KG construction (template extraction, parameter typing, CEE annotation, RDF graph building)
records.ss: template extraction is sensitive to the training data; entities cannot be identified if variable parts show too little variation (Sec. 6, p. 643).
records.ri: performance analysis and illustration rather than an accuracy evaluation.

records.use: Dataset introduction and analysis: execution-time comparison of RDFizers for dataset size, relation type, join duplicates and join selectivity configurations; motivating study on number of predicate-object maps, partitioning and duplicates.
records.dv: Synthetic testbed datasets (new; 1K, 10K and 50K rows, two tables; 30-column variant for the naive size test; varied relation types, join duplicates and join selectivity)
records.task: Benchmarking RML-based KG creation engines (SDM-RDFizer vs RMLMapper) across mapping and data variables
records.ss: only two RDFizers and RML are analysed; other engines and mapping languages left to future work (Sec. 6, p. 711).
records.ri: synthetic data; no real-world source evaluated.

records.use: Analysis and demonstration: ranked predicate alignments and count-related SPO queries over the three KBs (e.g., number of employees of Microsoft on DBpedia-mapped).
records.dv: Wikidata-truthy, DBpedia-mapped and DBpedia-raw (alignments also listed for Freebase)
records.task: Alignment of counting and enumerating predicates in KBs (demo)
records.dl: predicate constraints of general-purpose KBs are often limited to subproperty, domain and range constraints (p. 84).
records.ri: demonstration; alignment quality is not re-evaluated in this chapter.

records.loc: Sec. 1, Table 1, p. 203; Sec. 3, Table 2, pp. 205-206
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: Hits@1/Hits@3 of vector similarity (original and averaged class vectors) and CNN accuracy.
records.dv: DBpedia 2016-10 typing datasets (new; 59 classes x 500 entities, 86 classes x 2k, 81 classes x 4k)
records.task: Fine-grained entity typing with RDF2Vec (vector similarity and 1D CNN)
records.dl: most entities have only coarse-grained types (e.g., only 8.9% of 352,006 dbo:SportsTeam entities typed with its subclasses) (p. 203).

records.loc: Sec. 6, Table 1, Fig. 4, pp. 224-227
records.use: Testing (preliminary): cosine distances and clustering of column-header representations (syntactic vs embedding) to propose schema concepts.
records.dv: sWorm earthworm biodiversity dataset (sites, species, years; used in compiling sWorm data)
records.task: KG schema induction from tabular column headers (embedding-based clustering; PhD proposal)
records.ss: full conversion from CSV to KG cannot be fully automated; user intervention is needed to refine clusters (p. 224). T2Dv2, Limaye and SemTab 2019 are planned for later phases only (p. 224).

records.use: Dataset description and application: standards indexed in a triplestore and browsed by non-technical users; FAIR compliance described.
records.dv: Roche Global Data Standards Repository (clinical data standards aligned with CDISC as OWL/RDF ontologies and vocabularies; links to CDISC ontologies)
records.task: FAIR clinical data standards as Linked Data (Roche GDSR)
records.ri: industry report; no evaluation.

records.loc: Sec. III-A, p. 3; Tables I-II, p. 5 (PDF pages)
records.use: Analysis: ontology metrics Attribute Richness, Inheritance Richness and Relationship Richness of the proposed KGC vs MOE, RDISM, RDF-OSTSWR and ODCM (AR 1.2453, IR 1.4287, RR 0.4481).
records.dv: Environmental spatial and temporal datasets (lakes, rivers, agricultural zones, urban infrastructure; water level, air temperature, rainfall) in PostgreSQL/PostGIS
records.task: Ontology development via KG construction (PostGIS data, extended GeoSPARQL ontology, R2RML mappings, Jena reasoning)
records.ri: the datasets are not named, sourced or sized. the text states that KGC achieved better IR, but its IR (1.4287) is lower than RDISM (1.8653), RDF-OSTSWR (1.9765) and ODCM (1.6930) in Tables I-II (PDF p. 5).

records.loc: Sec. 5.2, Table 2, pp. 31-33; Table 3, p. 32
records.use: Training and testing: Hits@k and rank metrics of BoxEL vs TransE, TransH, DistMult, ELEm and EmEL++.
records.dv: Gene Ontology, GALEN and Anatomy ontologies (subclass axioms split 70/20/10)
records.task: EL++ ontology embedding for subsumption reasoning (ontology completion) with boxes
records.ss: classical KGEs fail on hits@k for these logical structures, as the authors note (p. 33).
records.ri: consolidated row (three ontologies).

records.loc: Sec. 5, Table 1, pp. 400-401; Tables 2-6, pp. 402-407
records.use: Training and testing: multi-class, multi-label and hierarchical (LPL) classification with RDF2vec walk variants and textual descriptions vs SOTA; unseen entities.
records.dv: DBpedia630k (630,000 entities, 14 classes; extended and split into DB-1, DB-2, DB-3 of 210,000 entities, 50/30/20) and FIGER (201,933 Freebase entities, 102 classes)
records.task: Entity type prediction with graph walks and entity descriptions (GRAND)
records.ri: DBpedia630k classes are coarse and non-overlapping; FIGER is Freebase-based.

records.use: Analysis: regularities in axioms and class frames, their sizes, nesting depth and Hasse-diagram depth across the corpus.
records.dv: BioPortal ontology corpus (736 ontologies collected; 657 in the experimental corpus)
records.task: Syntactic modelling regularities in biomedical ontologies (survey of ontology engineering practice)
records.ri: despite the title, this is an empirical corpus analysis, not a literature survey.

records.use: Testing: data coverage, knowledge coverage and user-friendliness of reshaped KG schemata vs four baselines; user study with tasks and questionnaires.
records.dv: Three Bosch resistance spot welding datasets D1, D2, D3 (relational tables with 121, 147 and 160 attributes; 1,000 welding operations selected from each) with an RSW domain ontology (210 class nodes, 191 datatype nodes)
records.task: Ontology reshaping for KG construction from relational manufacturing data (welding quality monitoring)
records.ri: proprietary industrial data; 1,000 operations per dataset sampled for comparison.

records.loc: Sec. 2, Table 1, pp. 62-63; Sec. 3, pp. 63-65
records.use: Analysis: gold-standard statistics compiled; STILTool loads annotations and gold standards to compute scores and error patterns.
records.dv: T2Dv2 (779 tables, 234 sharing instances with DBpedia), Limaye (over 6,000 tables, YAGO), Limaye200, Wikipedia tables (6,310 tables, Freebase), SemTab 2019 rounds 1-4
records.task: Semantic table interpretation evaluation (tables-to-KG matching: CEA, CTA, CPA)
records.dl: discrepancies among gold standards (target KG, table structure, storage format) hinder comparison (p. 63).
records.ss: consolidated row (several gold standards with the same role).
records.ri: the stated 234 tables sharing instances with DBpedia differ from the 237 on the T2Dv2 release page (descriptor KGD-0069); recorded as printed.

records.use: Application and demonstration: recognised entities linked and enriched with URIs and facts from multiple datasets, and the K most relevant datasets per entity retrieved.
records.dv: LODsyndesis (hundreds of linked datasets); DBpedia (via DBpedia Spotlight); Wikipedia (via WAT)
records.task: Entity extraction from text and enrichment from many linked datasets
records.ri: demonstration; no accuracy evaluation in this chapter.

records.use: Analysis and demonstration: drill-down evaluation of matcher results with on-the-fly recalculation.
records.dv: OAEI 2019 KnowledgeGraph track (more than 200,000 correspondences rendered)
records.task: Ontology matching results analysis (interactive evaluation dashboard)
records.ri: demonstration; no new matching results.

records.use: Application: legal texts annotated with links to ontologies and to related legal documents; similar documents retrieved.
records.dv: Semantic Finlex statutes, case law and keywords; Finnish legal vocabulary, Helsinki Term Bank, DBpedia, EuroVoc
records.task: Named entity linking of Finnish legal documents (Nelli-based annotation service Appi)
records.ss: currently Finnish only, though configurable for other languages (p. 210).
records.ri: no linking accuracy reported.

records.use: Analysis (summarising the author's prior studies): synonymy-, hypernymy- and embedding-based strategies compared across four KGs; KG embeddings evaluated on similarity gold standards; OAEI matchers performed comparatively badly on real-world financial data models.
records.dv: DBpedia, WebIsALOD, DBnary/Wiktionary and WordNet as background knowledge; OAEI data sets and SAP financial-services data models; three semantic similarity gold standards for KG embeddings
records.task: Schema and ontology matching with general-purpose background knowledge graphs (PhD proposal)
records.ss: no superior general-purpose KG was identified; strategy (synonymy) mattered more than source (p. 277).
records.ri: results are reported from earlier publications without tables here.

records.loc: Sec. 2, Listing 1, pp. 308-310

records.dv: Surface-Mount Technology data (SMD placement and AOI inspection JSON data converted to Parquet)
records.task: Semantic data integration of manufacturing data (SANSA DataLake, RML mappings over Parquet)
records.ri: industry report; data volumes and evaluation are not reported.

records.use: Training: entity recognition and linking model trained on pages with anchor markups, following a TAC KBP 2017 system; used for query entity linking in search.
records.dv: Anchor-text training data from SogouBaike and Wikipedia pages
records.task: Entity recognition and linking to the KG (Bi-LSTM-CRF)
records.ri: no evaluation figures are reported.

records.loc: Sec. 1, p. 197; Sec. 5, Table 1, p. 204; Tables 2-7, pp. 206-209
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: alignment results per snapshot vs retraining and inductive baselines; recall on alignments with new entities; effect of name attributes; time cost.
records.dv: DBP15K ZH-EN, JA-EN and FR-EN, each re-built into six growth snapshots (new; released)
records.task: Continual entity alignment for growing KGs
records.ri: growth is simulated by adding entities and triples to snapshots rather than taken from real KG versions.

records.loc: Sec. 5.2, Table 3, pp. 507-509; Table 4, p. 510
records.use: Testing: DAGOBAH-SL scores with and without Radar Station disambiguation.
records.dv: T2D, Limaye (both corrected and translated from DBpedia to Wikidata) and Tough Tables v2
records.task: Semantic table interpretation and entity disambiguation with KG embeddings (Radar Station)
records.dl: original T2D and Limaye contain annotation errors, corrected by the authors (p. 507).
records.ss: DBpedia entities translated to Wikidata via Wikipedia links, with manual correction (p. 507).

records.loc: Sec. 5, Table 1, p. 549; Tables 2-3, pp. 550-551
records.use: Testing: increase in connections (at least 450% for real datasets), connectivity analytics to 400 LOD datasets, and execution time with and without prefix index.
records.dv: Five real RDF datasets (3K to 1.5M triples) and two synthetic datasets, connected against LODsyndesis (over 412 million entities and 2 billion triples from 400 LOD datasets)
records.task: Strengthening connectivity of an RDF dataset to the LOD cloud (LODChain: URI equivalence, linking and enrichment)
records.dl: the real datasets have few links and few prefixes known to LODsyndesis (in the worst case only 26.4% of URIs share a known prefix) (p. 549).

records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: results of non-ML and ML-based OM systems on equivalence and subsumption matching.

records.task: Biomedical ontology matching for equivalence and subsumption (ML-friendly resources; OAEI 2022 Bio-ML track)
records.ss: motivated by OAEI limitations: limited evaluation of subsumption mappings, suboptimal reference mappings and limited support for ML-based systems (pp. 575, 577).

records.loc: Sec. 4.4, Tables 4-5, p. 20; Figs. 12-13, p. 21; Table 6, p. 22
records.use: Training and testing: MR, MRR and Hits@1/3/10 of text-enhanced GAT vs TransH for head, tail and relation prediction (relation prediction MR 71 to 33, MRR 0.597 to 0.721).

records.use: Training and testing: mean rank and Hit@10 over eleven parameter combinations; TransD selected, then retrained on all data.

records.task: KG embedding for event similarity (TransD vs TransR)
records.ri: tail-entity ranking only; the final model is trained on all data, so no held-out score is reported for it.

records.loc: Sec. 3.2.3, Table 9, p. 19; Table 10, p. 20; Table 11, pp. 20-21
records.use: Training and testing: MRR, MR and Hits@1/3/10; ConvE best (MRR 0.454, Hits@10 0.574).
records.dv: ISLKG split 84:7:7 (297,700 train / 24,231 validation / 24,231 test triples)

records.use: Dataset construction, training and testing: KG built from IMDB attributes linked to MovieLens 1M; time-ordered 80/20 split; RKGE compared with MostPop, BPRMF, NCF, LIBFM, HeteRS, HeteRec, GraphLF and CKE on Prec@1/5/10 and MRR@10 for all users and cold-start users (<5 ratings); path-length and pooling analyses; interpretability example (Fig. 5).
records.dv: IM-1M (new combination: MovieLens 1M ratings linked to IMDB movie attributes by title and release date; 6,040 users, 3,382 items, 756,684 ratings; KG 18,920 entities, 11 entity types, 800,261 links, 10 link types)
records.task: KG-enhanced top-N recommendation (recurrent encoding of user-item KG paths)
records.ss: CKE's textual and visual parts were removed because such information is unavailable in the datasets (p. 6). cold-start users have very few KG paths, which the authors give as the reason for smaller gains (p. 8).
records.ri: the IMDB linkage and resulting KG are not released.

records.loc: Sec. 4.1, Table 2, p. 6; Figs. 3-4, Table 3, p. 7 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: as for IM-1M, with the published train/test split; all-users and cold-start views.
records.dv: Yelp Challenge Dataset (37,940 users, 11,516 businesses, 229,178 ratings; business-information KG 46,606 entities, 7 entity types, 302,937 links, 6 link types; original train/test split)
records.task: KG-enhanced top-N recommendation (recurrent encoding of user-item KG paths)
records.dl: Yelp is much sparser than IM-1M (0.052% vs 3.704% density), and the authors expect lower performance on it (p. 6).
records.ss: future work to consider entity-type taxonomy (p. 8).

records.loc: Sec. 4.1, Table 1, p. 6; Table 2, p. 7; Table 3, p. 7; Sec. 4.3-4.4, pp. 8-9; Sec. 5, Fig. 6, pp. 9-10 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset construction, training and testing: PGPR compared with BPR, BPR-HFT, VBPR, TransRec, DeepCoNN, CKE and JRL on NDCG, Recall, Hit Rate and Precision at top-10; valid-path statistics, ablations on reward and action pruning, sample-size sensitivity; qualitative case study of reasoning paths (Beauty, others).
records.dv: Amazon e-commerce review datasets [McAuley et al., ref. 7]: CDs & Vinyl, Clothing, Cell Phones, Beauty, each turned into a KG with 5 entity types (user, item, feature, brand, category) and 7 relations; review feature words filtered by TF-IDF; random 70/30 purchase split
records.task: Explainable recommendation by RL path reasoning over a user-item KG (KGRE-Rec)
records.dl: Mention and Described_by dominate the relations and link to feature words that may be redundant or less meaningful; low-salience features are removed by TF-IDF (p. 6).
records.ss: paths limited to three hops from user to item (p. 7). about half of the sampled paths are valid (p. 7). consolidated row (four category datasets, identical role).

records.loc: Sec. 3.1, p. 83; Data split, p. 85; Sec. 4, pp. 85-88
records.use: Dataset construction, training and testing: BART-base and T5-base fine-tuned on each of 12 syntaxes (RDF/XML, N-Triples, Turtle, JSON-LD and variants incl. 'Turtle Light'); validity of produced triples, F1 variants, learning velocity, stability and divergence, and resource use compared.
records.dv: DBpedia snapshot 2022-09 dbo:Person subgraphs aligned with Wikipedia abstracts (filtered to values found in the abstract and to graphs valid against a SHACL shape; 5,000 examples in 5-fold rotation of 4,000 train / 1,000 test, plus 250 disjoint evaluation examples)
records.task: Relation extraction from text into RDF: datatype properties of dbo:Person, generated in 12 RDF linearisations
records.dl: in a 1,000-entity sample, 80% of triples have values found in the abstract but only 45% of entities have a description graph valid against the shape (p. 83).
records.ss: datatype properties only, to avoid entity linking (p. 83). T5 and BART were partly pre-trained on Wikipedia, so they may have seen the facts; results depend on the tokeniser (p. 88).
records.ri: the full filtered set (1,833,493 entities, 3,249,446 triples) was reduced to 5,000 examples (p. 83).

records.loc: Abstract, p. 129; Sec. 2.1, p. 131; Sec. 3, pp. 131-132
records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: GPT-4 extracts entities and relations from segmented PDFs and generates Cypher; entity recognition accuracy 96.5% and relationship extraction 95.2% on the 500-entity validation set; operational figures (retrieval time, 2,000 user queries) reported.
records.dv: AddQual turbine-repair multi-modal KG (internal; 131 nodes, 148 relationships: components, images, repair rules, measurements, actions) with a 500-entity validation set
records.task: LLM-based construction of a multi-modal maintenance KG from unstructured repair documents (Neo4j, Text2Cypher)
records.ss: authors call for robust data validation frameworks as future work (p. 132).
records.ri: the 88% robustness figure is a HELM score for GPT-4, not a measurement on this KG (p. 132); the validation protocol and annotators are not described beyond 'domain experts'.

records.use: Training and source KG: an in-house LLM fine-tuned on the proprietary talent graph extracts skills, capabilities and responsibilities from job descriptions and returns canonical-skill URIs; resulting graphs are persisted with provenance and used in production for candidate matching.
records.dv: Beamery HR domain model and talent graph (proprietary; SKOS taxonomy of canonical skills; job descriptions stored as named graphs)
records.task: KG generation from job descriptions: LLM concept extraction and reconciliation to a canonical skills taxonomy
records.ss: no quantitative evaluation; authors list possible wrong extractions, hallucinations, wrong reconciliation and concepts missing from the taxonomy (p. 146). linking to ESCO or O*NET left for future work (p. 146).

records.use: Dataset introduction: JSON collection data converted to Turtle with rdflib scripts (Art Object, Person, Multimedia classes); served from a restricted read-only Fuseki endpoint on Linked Data Finland and explored with Sampo-UI faceted search and charts.
records.dv: ArtSampo KG, initial version (about 1,100,000 triples; over 58,000 art objects and 6,400 artists from the Finnish National Gallery open data: Ateneum, Kiasma, Sinebrychoff)
records.task: Cultural-heritage KG construction from museum collection metadata, with a faceted semantic portal
records.dl: initial data model with most metadata as literals; final model and reuse of existing vocabularies still to be designed (p. 161). single source; integration with other museums, Wikidata, ULAN and other Sampo KGs is future work (pp. 162-163).
records.ss: release as LOD is a stated goal, the current endpoint is restricted (pp. 160, 163).

records.use: Dataset and ontology introduction: six-step ETL (action, cleaning, update, stash, endpoint, analysis) maps feeds in formats such as LIDO and MEI to CTO; data served via a public SPARQL endpoint, SHMARQL and a dashboard.
records.dv: NFDI4Culture-KG: Research Information Graph (resource metadata) and Research Data Graph (harvested content metadata of data feeds), modelled with NFDIcore and the Culture Ontology (CTO) linking to GND, Wikidata and ICONCLASS
records.task: Harvesting cultural-heritage metadata from legacy repositories into a unified KG (ETL workflow, lightweight ontology)
records.dl: much NFDI4Culture data still unindexed in legacy silos (p. 179).
records.ss: report on ongoing extension; no evaluation of harvesting coverage or quality (pp. 179-182). CTO deliberately lightweight compared with CIDOC-CRM, not representing fine-grained aspects (p. 181).

records.loc: Sec. 2, pp. 184-186; Figs. 1-2; Data and Software Availability, p. 186
records.use: Dataset introduction: records harvested via OAI-PMH, sitemaps, feeds and DataCite/GitHub/GitLab APIs, uplifted with inferable types, de-duplicated with Prefect, loaded into Virtuoso and Solr, and exposed through SPARQL, web search and API.
records.dv: Helmholtz Knowledge Graph, first release (2.15 million metadata records from 32 Helmholtz data providers; 72 million triples; 16.35 million typed entities; 793k entities with a PID or URL; schema.org/JSON-LD)
records.task: Aggregation of research-output metadata into an institutional KG (harvesting, semantic uplifting, de-duplication)
records.dl: metadata often lacks types and PIDs, producing duplicated blank-node instances that impair search (pp. 185-186). DOI PIDs are used heterogeneously for data and scholarly communications (p. 186).
records.ss: entity resolution and type inference by logic and ML are future work (p. 186).
records.ri: Fig. 1 caption reports 2.26 million main entities, the text 2.15 million records (pp. 184-185); these may count different things.

records.use: Dataset introduction: OCR, co-reference resolution (English), post-OCR correction and sentence splitting; SPRING (EN) and USeA (IT) AMR parsing; AMR2FRED conversion to RDF/OWL named graphs; Framester alignment to DBpedia, Wikidata and VerbAtlas; AMR graphs filtered by back-translation (BLEURT for EN, cosine similarity >= 0.90 for IT).
records.dv: MusicBO corpus (part of the Polifonia Textual Corpus; 137 texts in four languages, 1700 to present; 47 English and 51 Italian documents processed) and the resulting MusicBO KG (531,073 triples from 7,557 filtered sentence-AMR pairs)
records.task: Text-to-KG construction from multilingual diachronic historical texts via AMR (Text2AMR2FRED)
records.dl: copyright prevents full disclosure of the corpus; only metadata to reproduce it is released (p. 213). text2AMR parsers may be inaccurate on historic and OCRed text and no standard benchmark exists; filtering kept 7,557 of 62,377 pairs (pp. 214-215).
records.ss: co-reference resolution only for English (p. 214).
records.ri: Table 2 prints counts with dots as thousands separators (e.g. 531.073), read here as 531,073 (p. 214).

records.use: Dataset introduction: Estonian XML statutes transformed to RDF with the LawSampo model, statutes linked to EU directives, keywords extracted with EuroVoc and documents classified by life events; published on Linked Data Finland and searched through Sampo-UI faceted search, timelines and machine translation.
records.dv: FinEstLawSampo KG (nearly 13,000 Finnish and Estonian statutes and 5,000 EU directives from the EU Cellar; LawSampo data model; EuroVoc keywords; Finnish and Estonian life-event classes)
records.task: Cross-border multilingual legislation KG (aggregation, EuroVoc keyword extraction, life-event classification) with a faceted portal
records.ss: no formal end-user testing; machine translation judged only by informal testing (pp. 246, 248). Sampo-UI scalability depends on data-model complexity, with about one million instances in the largest Sampo systems (p. 248).
records.ri: no evaluation of the keyword extraction or classification is reported.

records.use: Dataset introduction: museum CSV data converted to RDF with ontologies derived from the data, reusing the FindSampo conversion script; served openly from Linked Data Finland and analysed with faceted search and map visualisations (mint-to-findsite arcs).
records.dv: CoinSampo KG (about 18,000 numismatic citizen finds reported to the National Museum of Finland 2013-2023; mints mapped to Wikidata, find municipalities to YSO Places)
records.task: Cultural-heritage KG of citizen coin finds with lightweight ontologies linked to Wikidata and YSO Places, and a Sampo-UI portal
records.ss: some visualisations need specific semantics such as mint coordinates; meaningful comparison with other datasets requires harmonisation effort (p. 299).
records.ri: no evaluation; demonstration of an open data service.

records.use: Analysis (demonstration): SPARQL queries over MusicXML files extract melodies into pandas DataFrames; note trigrams are counted and a probability mass function compared with the showcase's trigramAnalysis.csv.
records.dv: SPARQL Anything showcase-musicxml MusicXML scores (AltDeu10 folder) and the example1.json TV-series file (demonstration inputs)
records.task: KG construction from heterogeneous files via Facade-X (Python library and CLI for SPARQL Anything)
records.ri: demonstration paper; the musicology scenario reproduces an existing showcase and no performance comparison with the Java tool is reported.

records.use: Dataset introduction: spreadsheet annotations converted with OpenRefine and QuickStatements into Wikidata, enriched with GitHub activity metadata, and exposed through a visualisation and search page.
records.dv: Semantic Tool Hub data (new; almost 150 RDF-related tools curated from recent ISWC/ESWC papers, the Awesome Semantic Web list and the OntoCommons report, categorised by a new taxonomy and transformed to Wikidata statements)
records.task: Community-driven documentation of Semantic Web tools in Wikidata (taxonomy, curation, GitHub metadata)
records.dl: the Awesome Semantic Web list contains many outdated tools (p. 312).
records.ss: data curated manually by the author of the demo; community updating is a hope, not yet in place (p. 314). scope limited to tools for RDF-based technologies (p. 312).

records.use: Dataset introduction: instances mapped with RML to ODTA domain specifications (SHACL), verified on import, enriched by distance-based geo-linking to e-charging stations and public transport stops, and served through an API, SPARQL and a search widget.
records.dv: German Tourism Knowledge Graph (GTKG; data from the regional marketing organisations of 16 German states, updated daily since May 2023; on 07/03/2024 about 239K events, 118K points of interest, 23K trails, 25K lodging, 70K local businesses, 20K food establishments)
records.task: Stakeholder-driven construction and integration of a national tourism KG (schema.org-based domain specifications, SHACL verification, geo-linking)
records.dl: provider-specific instance identifiers are not always dereferenceable, so a wrapper URI is provided (p. 319). licences are set per instance (typically CC BY-SA); no full-graph dump yet, only per-instance downloads (p. 319).
records.ss: migration to the February 2024 ODTA release still ongoing (fn. 5, p. 317).
records.dom: Geospatial, urban and environment; Business, e-commerce and tourism

records.use: Analysis (demonstration): RMLdoc validates and queries the mapping graph and writes Markdown documentation with metadata, prefixes, rule sets and Mermaid diagrams for the GTFS-Madrid-Bench mappings.
records.dv: GTFS-Madrid-Bench mapping subset (demonstration example)
records.task: Human-readable documentation of declarative KG construction mappings (R2RML, RML, YARRRML)
records.ss: named graphs, full compliance with the new RML modules and Triples-Map-level metadata are future work (p. 329).
records.ri: demonstration only; no user evaluation of documentation usefulness.

records.loc: Sec. 3, p. 5; Table 1, p. 6; Sec. 4, p. 7; Tables 2-3, pp. 8-9; Table 5, p. 11
records.use: Testing: candidate CQs generated by gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 and gpt-4-0613 from extracted ontology triples with three prompt templates and two temperature settings (0.0, 0.7) are matched to the design CQs with SBERT; precision, recall, F1, unmatched design CQs and cross-prompt overlap reported.
records.dv: CQ benchmark: design CQs of four ontologies from CORAL and Wisniewski et al. (2019): Video Game (66 CQs, 57 triples), African Wildlife (14, 26), Dem@care (107, 146), VICINITY Core (57, 226)
records.task: Competency question (CQ) retrofitting from ontology triples with LLMs
records.ss: only two OpenAI GPT models; a wider study is stated as in preparation (pp. 5, 11). four ontologies selected by three criteria (different developers, domains, many published CQs) (p. 5).
records.ri: recall is defined with unmatched benchmark CQs labelled as true negatives (p. 7), and recall is at least 0.96 throughout, so precision carries the comparison. p. 8 calls CP=0.7 the deterministic value, which contradicts the definition on p. 7 (0.0 deterministic).

records.use: Testing: wine ontologies generated by GPT-3.5 with zero-shot prompting, Stanford-guide prompts and the NeOn-GPT workflow are compared with the gold standard by structural metrics (OntoMetrics, Protege: axioms, classes, properties, individuals), class hierarchy and pre-/post-inference behaviour (HermiT).
records.dv: Stanford (Protege) Wine ontology, used as gold standard
records.task: Ontology learning from natural-language domain descriptions with LLM prompt pipelines (NeOn methodology)
records.ss: single domain case study (wine) (pp. 36, 41). LLM-generated class expressions limited to subsumption without conjunction or disjunction, and property restrictions mostly hasValue, so the generated ontology does not reach the gold standard's expressivity (p. 43).
records.ri: comparison is by counts and hierarchy inspection, with no alignment-based precision or recall against the gold standard.

records.loc: Sec. 2, p. 63; Table 1, p. 64; Tables 2-5, pp. 66-68; Sec. 5, pp. 67-68
records.use: Training (demonstration selection, fine-tuning gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 and RoBERTa on down-sampled train sets) and testing: Micro-F1 of zero-shot prompt variants (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, SOLAR), random vs similar demonstrations, and fine-tuned models on CPA and CTA.
records.dv: SOTAB V2 CPA (test 2,340 columns, 108 schema.org terms) and SOTAB V2 CTA (test 609 tables, 1,851 columns, 82 schema.org terms); down-sampled training sets
records.task: Semantic table annotation: column property annotation (CPA) and column type annotation (CTA) with LLMs
records.ss: original large training sets deliberately down-sampled to simulate low-resource settings (p. 63).
records.ri: the text gives 595 test tables for SOTAB V2 CPA (p. 63) while Table 1 gives 565 (p. 64).

records.loc: Sec. 2, p. 63; Table 1, p. 64; Tables 2-4, pp. 66-67
records.use: Testing and dataset introduction (T2Dv2 CTA): zero-shot and few-shot Micro-F1; out-of-vocabulary test for models fine-tuned on SOTAB V2.
records.dv: T2Dv2 CPA (manually verified version; 80 test tables labelled with 48 DBpedia properties) and T2Dv2 CTA (new; built by mapping the CPA DBpedia properties to DBpedia classes)
records.task: Semantic table annotation: generalisation of CPA and CTA to an unseen vocabulary
records.ss: models fine-tuned for one task and dataset lose performance on the unseen T2Dv2 sets; joint CTA+CPA fine-tuning on the larger set generalises better (p. 68).
records.ri: T2Dv2 CTA labels are derived from CPA property labels rather than annotated independently. the text gives 80 T2Dv2 CPA test tables (p. 63), Table 1 gives 82 (p. 64).

records.loc: Sec. 4.1, p. 75; Table 3, p. 75; Sec. 4.3, p. 77; Table 5, p. 78
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: GPT-3.5 and open LLMs up to 13B (DPO, Solar, UNA, Zephyr) generate CQs from classes, classes plus properties or a schema summary, with 0 or more example CQs; precision of generated CQs whose SentenceBERT cosine similarity to an author CQ exceeds 0.6.
records.dv: LLM4KE ontology-CQ dataset (new; versioned copies of five ontologies with author CQs and SPARQL authoring tests normalised to YAML: DemCare (via CQ2SPARQLOWL), NORIA-O, DOREMUS, Odeuropa, Polifonia)
records.task: Competency question generation from an existing ontology with LLMs
records.dl: no authoring tests found for Polifonia (Table 3, p. 75).
records.ss: precision only, with an empirically chosen threshold; generated CQs not in the ground truth may still be valid and need an expert panel (p. 77). ontologies with more classes were queried more often because of batching (p. 78). open models limited to 13B parameters for resource reasons (p. 76).
records.dom: Biomedical and health; Industry, engineering and energy; Cultural heritage and humanities

records.use: Testing: ontology testing evaluated as classification of supported vs unsupported CQs with gpt-3.5-turbo (accuracy 87.5%, P 88%, R 85.7%); user-story creation and CQ extraction/clustering evaluated with Likert questionnaires (6 music experts, 8 ontology engineers) replicating the Music Meta engineering.
records.dv: Music Meta ontology (OWL) with its 28 manually produced CQs, extended with 28 negative CQs; Polifonia user stories (Linka - Music Knowledge story) and ground-truth material from the Music Meta project
records.task: Conversational ontology engineering with LLMs: requirement elicitation, CQ extraction and clustering, ontology testing
records.ss: preliminary evaluation with small participant groups (N = 6 and N = 8) (p. 108). LLMs have limited or obsolete knowledge in specialised domains; persona bias not addressed (pp. 109-110).
records.ri: negative CQs were written by the authors, so the classification test depends on their construction.

records.use: Ontology introduction and application: data attributes are matched to ADOn concepts by Levenshtein, Jaro and Jaccard similarity of names and descriptions to concept labels and definitions, during or after upload; annotations support semantic search and dataset linking.
records.dv: AquaDiva Ontology (ADOn; 78,840 axioms, 8,892 concepts, 245 object properties; built by fusing existing ontologies with JOYCE) and CRC AquaDiva data-portal datasets
records.task: Semi-automatic semantic annotation of scientific dataset attributes with a domain ontology
records.ss: demonstration only; no evaluation of recommendation quality reported (pp. 166-167).
records.ri: the dataset examples (DS1 with 50 attributes, DS2 with 13) are illustrations, not an evaluation set. ontology sizes are printed as 78.840 and 8.892 and read here with the dot as thousands separator (p. 166).

records.use: Testing: GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview, greedy decoding) generates ontologies in four trials (generic prompt, with patterns, metacognitive prompting, both); outputs compared with the reference ontology by OntoMetrics counts, OWL axiom types, OOPS! pitfalls and expert analysis.
records.dv: African Wildlife Ontology subset of the CQ/SPARQL-OWL gold standard of Wisniewski et al. (14 competency questions), with eight content ontology design patterns from ontologydesignpatterns.org
records.task: Ontology generation from competency questions with metacognitive prompting and ontology design patterns
records.ss: single use case of 14 CQs (p. 261). CQs given in groups because of the output token limit (p. 262). generated ontologies lack property hierarchies and show annotation and domain/range errors; authors judge them not ready for real-world use (pp. 263-264). expert analysis by one ontology engineer (pp. 261-263).

records.task: Ontology matching with retrieval-augmented LLMs (LLMs4OM)
records.ss: zero-shot only, equivalence matching only; about 50 runs per dataset, complete results in supplementary material not in the PDF (p. 29).

records.use: Testing (zero-shot): four retrievers (TFIDF, sentence-BERT, SPECTER2, text-embedding-ada; recall at top-k 5/10/20) and seven LLMs judge candidate concept pairs with concept, concept-parent and concept-children representations; precision, recall and F1 of equivalence matches compared with the best OAEI 2023 systems.

records.use: Testing (zero-shot): four retrievers (TFIDF, sentence-BERT, SPECTER2, text-embedding-ada; recall at top-k 5/10/20) and seven LLMs judge candidate concept pairs with concept, concept-parent and concept-children representations; precision, recall and F1 of equivalence matches compared with the best OAEI 2023 systems.

records.use: Testing (zero-shot): four retrievers (TFIDF, sentence-BERT, SPECTER2, text-embedding-ada; recall at top-k 5/10/20) and seven LLMs judge candidate concept pairs with concept, concept-parent and concept-children representations; precision, recall and F1 of equivalence matches compared with the best OAEI 2023 systems.

records.use: Source data and integration: a converter with a schema matcher (labels, comments and definitions; ChatGPT prompting and embedding cosine similarity) maps oai_dc, DC terms and DC elements fields to DCAT before the Piveau harvester ingests them.
records.dv: Metadata of the DSpace repositories of HU Berlin, FU Berlin and TU Berlin (oai_dc with institution-specific vocabularies), converted to DCAT for the Berlin Open Science Platform; NFDI4Cat Zenodo community and BasCat Dataverse named as further harvested sources
records.task: Schema alignment of harvested repository metadata to DCAT for a research-data meta portal
records.ss: schema-matching experiments are only referenced to the GitHub repository, with no results in the chapter (p. 205).
records.ri: no measurement of conversion correctness or coverage is reported.

records.loc: Sec. 3, pp. 240-241; Sec. 4 and Table 1, pp. 241-242
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: training and validation alignments used to tune the confidence thresholds of Matcha, LogMap and OLaLa (OAEI 2023), with partial or complete input-alignment assumptions; micro-averaged precision, recall and F1 on the test split vs untuned systems.
records.dv: OAEI ML dataset (new; reference alignments of the Anatomy, BioDiv, Knowledge Graph and Bio-ML tracks split 20/10/70, stratified by entity type, relation type and difficulty; positives only)
records.task: Ontology and KG matching with machine learning: train/validation/test splits for online model generation
records.dl: no negative examples provided; systems must generate them assuming one-to-one, duplicate-free graphs (p. 241).
records.ss: only test cases with at least 350 reference correspondences included, so the Conference track is not covered (pp. 241, 243). Knowledge Graph track results are instance matches; OLaLa cannot match instances (p. 242).
records.ri: consolidated row (four tracks, identical role).

records.ss: MultiModalQA questions that need table evidence are excluded because there is no table encoder (p. 11). PCST coefficients are fixed after development tuning rather than learned (pp. 6, 17).

records.task: Spatio-temporal KG question answering
records.dl: few interval facts in YAGO15k and strict generation rules limit the number of double-time-constraint questions (p. 4). questions are template-generated and LLM-paraphrased rather than user-authored (p. 4).
records.ss: authors state there is still considerable room for improvement (Conclusion, p. 8).

records.ri: the stated 13.5k questions (7k/3.2k/3.2k) differ from the 16,181 questions (9,708 / 3,236 / 3,237) of the introducing release (descriptor KGD-0054); recorded as printed.

records.loc: Sec. 4, p. 5; Sec. 4.2 and Table 1, p. 6; Sec. 4.3, p. 6; Tables 2-3, p. 7
records.use: Source KG construction and testing: conversation histories are ingested into a temporal KG with gpt-4o-mini; the 20 most relevant edges and entity nodes are retrieved as context; accuracy, latency and context tokens compared with MemGPT, session summaries and full-context baselines (gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4o), with a per-question-type breakdown on LongMemEval.

records.task: Temporal KG-based agent memory: retrieval of facts and entity summaries from a KG built from conversations
records.dl: authors judge DMR inadequate: small scale (about 60 messages per conversation), single-turn fact-retrieval questions, ambiguous phrasing and poor representation of enterprise use cases (p. 6).
records.ss: experiments cover a subset of Graphiti's search functionality (p. 5). MemGPT results with gpt-4o-mini could not be reproduced (p. 6).

records.loc: Sec. II.A, p. 401; Sec. III.A, pp. 403-404; Table I, p. 405
records.use: Dataset introduction, source KG construction and testing: graph-based answering with Qwen2.5-VL-32B compared with a Vector RAG baseline over the same 300 texts; F1 for mining and tracing, accuracy for verification, with the 40 fallacious articles simulating corrupted KG construction.
records.dv: Authors' test set of 300 international hotspot events sourced from Wikipedia (all after February 2025) with three query categories and human-annotated reference answers, plus 40 LLM-generated articles with logical fallacies; MMKG built in Neo4j from the same source data
records.task: Social media public opinion analysis over an LLM-built multimodal KG: information mining, tracing and verification (misinformation detection)
records.dl: events limited to those after February 2025 to avoid overlap with LLM training corpora (p. 403).
records.ss: authors report limited ability to detect deep logical fallacies such as causal inversion, and a temporal mismatch between fast-evolving events and KG updates (p. 404; Sec. III.B, p. 405).
records.ri: one baseline; test set not released.

records.use: Analysis (case study): generated plan assessed by field completion accuracy, knowledge reuse rate, generation time, cosine similarity to expert templates, and ratings by three senior engineers (Cohen's Kappa reported).
records.dv: TDFPC MMKG (authors'); one case project
records.task: Construction technology disclosure plan generation: case matching, graph-based multi-hop inference and template mapping over the MMKG
records.ss: validation on a single project without comparison to manual drafting or BIM-only workflows, and scope limited to deep excavation projects (pp. 25, 29).

records.loc: Sec. III.B, p. 3; Sec. V, p. 7; Table I, p. 7; Tables II-III, p. 8 (PDF pages)
records.use: Source KG and training/testing: ConceptNet supplies structured knowledge for automatically generated mission-specific KGs whose node embeddings feed the GNN; frame-level VAD and VAR evaluated on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence (AUC, mAUC, AP) against state-of-the-art methods; GPU-memory comparison.

records.task: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection and recognition with mission-specific KGs and a hierarchical multimodal GNN
records.ss: authors name the inability to capture long-term dependencies (classification over 30 frames) as the primary limitation (p. 7). ShanghaiTech not used because some anomaly classes occur only in training (p. 7). lags behind state of the art for VAD on UCF-Crime and VAR on XD-Violence, attributed to constraints of the KG generation framework (p. 7).

records.loc: Sec. 4, pp. 4-5; Table 1, p. 5; Table 2, p. 7; Tables 4-6, p. 8
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: LLM-parsed scene graphs verified by annotators and senior reviewers, then generalised into rule-consistent graph variants; Qwen2.5 and Qwen2.5-VL variants with stepwise scene-prior injection and multimodal fusion evaluated on decision accuracy, rare or unseen complaint types, robustness to missing or corrupted evidence, and ablations.

records.task: Multimodal complaint decision making with Scene Knowledge Graph priors
records.dl: the scene graphs and QA pairs are produced by an internal LLM-based pipeline with human verification and graph generalisation (p. 4).
records.ri: release of the dataset is not stated.

records.loc: Sec. 5.1, pp. 15-17; Fig. 5, p. 16; Listing 1, p. 17
records.use: Analysis (demonstration): MeGraS served as the graph store of LifeGraph 5 in LSC'25 for known-item search, QA and ad-hoc tasks; a case study answers an LSC'25 QA task with a SPARQL query that uses a derived OCR relation.

records.task: Content-aware multimodal KG storage and querying: extended SPARQL with derived (on-demand) relations such as OCR, captions and embeddings
records.ss: authors note the deterministic representation (extracted features stored as static triples without confidence), the semantic gap, and the lack of a cost-based query optimiser (pp. 20-21).
records.ri: no quantitative results of the LSC participation or of store performance are reported in this use case.

records.loc: Sec. 6-6.1, pp. 12-13; Listing 2, p. 13; Secs. 6.2-6.3, pp. 14-16; Fig. 4, p. 14; Tables 1-2, p. 15; Tables 3-4, p. 17; Table 5, p. 18 (PDF pages)
records.use: Analysis: patterns discovered in the sampled graph were presented as SPARQL queries with natural-language descriptions and in a pattern browser to 13 social and economic history experts (of 42 invited), who rated novelty, validity, utility and interpretability in an online questionnaire.

records.dl: the dataset cannot be shared because of the sensitivity of the data (Sec. 6.1, p. 13).
records.ss: a 100,000-person sample of over 5.5 million people is used; the authors assume the same patterns emerge (p. 13). 13 participants, low agreement on the pattern ratings (Kendall's W = 0.14) and 46% of participants gave themselves the lowest confidence score (pp. 14-15).
records.ri: evaluation measures perceived interestingness, not a reproducible benchmark.

records.loc: Sec. 2, Fig. 1, Table 1, Fig. 2, PDF pp. 1-2 (PDF pages)

records.ri: no quality or correctness evaluation of the KG or of the inferred triples is reported.

records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: five-fold cross-validation of BERT-BiLSTM-CRF vs CRF (CRF++ 0.54) and BiLSTM-CRF (word2vec) on recognising the core knowledge points (P/R/F1); new knowledge points occurring more than three times manually checked for accuracy.
records.dv: Computer-science subject teaching dataset M (syllabuses, textbooks, lesson plans; size '6M', 8,834 labelled sentences) and online encyclopedia dataset N (size '500M', 48,657 labelled sentences), labelled by distant supervision with 322 core knowledge points
records.task: Subject knowledge-point recognition for educational KG construction (BERT-BiLSTM-CRF, distant supervision)
records.ss: knowledge-point terms with complex structure cause recognition errors (e.g., 'Extended Cartesian Product' recognised as 'Cartesian Product') (p. 34). distant-supervision labels were inspected manually and judged to contain little noise (p. 32).
records.ri: the size units of M and N ('6M', '500M') are not stated.

records.loc: Sec. 4.2, Table 5, Figs. 5-6, pp. 34-35; Sec. 4.3, Fig. 7, p. 35
records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: 3,234 recognised knowledge points; semantic similarity (window n, threshold s), PMI (threshold t) and NGD thresholds tuned by P/R/F1 (best n = 20, s = 0.8, t = 4, NGD = 1); new points more than three edges from the core discarded; final graph visualised with Gephi and sigma.js.
records.dv: Computer-science subject KG (final: 2,207 knowledge-point nodes, 3,122 edges) built from datasets M and N; Normalized Google Distance computed from Baidu search hits
records.task: Educational subject KG construction: knowledge-point association assessment and bootstrapped expansion
records.ss: distance-based filtering of new knowledge points is a heuristic to be studied further (p. 35). applications (learning assessment, navigation, recommendation) are future work (p. 35).
records.ri: how the gold standard for association F1 was obtained is not described.

records.loc: Methods, pp. 2-3; Table 2, p. 3; p. 4; Figs. 3-4, pp. 4-5
records.use: Source data and dataset introduction: Qwen2-72B converts each abstract into JSON nodes and relations, imported via Cypher and linked to publication metadata; 100 extraction results manually reviewed (98% accurate and comprehensive, F1 0.9898); KG used for literature querying and trend and metal-application mining compared with Web of Science searches.
records.dv: Web of Science abstracts and metadata of more than 100,000 articles published before 8 May 2024 (MOF 68,400; COF 21,776; HOF 15,203); resulting KG-FM in Neo4j (2.53 million nodes, 4.01 million relationships)
records.task: LLM-based KG construction from scientific abstracts (framework materials: MOFs, COFs, HOFs)
records.dl: only abstracts and publication details are processed, not full texts (p. 2).
records.ri: extraction quality is estimated from 100 reviewed outputs; the KG-vs-Web of Science discrepancy in Fig. 4 is attributed by the authors to hidden links found by the KG (p. 5) but is not checked against ground truth.
records.dom: Scholarly and education; Industry, engineering and energy

records.loc: Sec. 3.2-3.3, pp. 3-4; Sec. 4.1, p. 4; Table 1, Sec. 4.2-4.3, Table 2, p. 5 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction and analysis: E-OED framework (Vietnamese SimCSE, UMAP, HDBSCAN, automatic labelling) yields 284 clusters and about 372 intents; Sentence-BERT two-stage retrieval with TF-IDF reranking links intents to policies at threshold 0.32; 53 intents receive no policy link, of which 22 are missed links.
records.dv: FAQ_HCMUT_vni (over 200,000 Vietnamese FAQs from the HCMUT HelpDesk system); HCMUT policy documents; resulting intent-policy KG in Neo4j (243 intent and 237 policy entities; 613 relations)
records.task: Educational KG construction: open intent (entity) discovery from FAQs and embedding-based relation discovery between intents and policies
records.ss: many clusters are noisy or duplicated and a substantial number of intents remain undiscovered (p. 5). clustering and labelling suffer from inadequate Vietnamese NLP toolkits and named entities in sentences (p. 5). due to resource and time constraints only intent and policy entities were linked (p. 4).
records.ri: the KG is described as handcrafted from the intent-discovery results; no KG size beyond these counts is given.
records.dom: Scholarly and education; Legal and public sector

records.loc: p. 2; Sec. 3, pp. 4-6; Sec. 4, Fig. 1, Tables 2-3, pp. 6-8; Sec. 5 (entity resolution), p. 9; Sec. 6.1, pp. 10-11
records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: recipes converted to RDF, USDA tables converted with the Semantic Data Dictionary, ingredients linked to USDA records and FoodOn classes by normalised string cosine similarity; KG checked by answering SPARQL competency questions (recipes containing given ingredients, vegan recipes via the ingredient hierarchy).
records.dv: FoodKG (over one million recipes, 67 million triples) built from Recipe1M (over 1 million recipes from recipe sites), the USDA National Nutrient Database for Standard Reference (about 8,000 food records) and a FoodOn subset extracted with Ontofox
records.task: Food KG construction and integration (recipes, ingredients, nutrients, food taxonomy; semantic ETL and entity linking)
records.dl: FoodOn lacks nutritional information and links to real recipes (p. 5); the USDA data is generic rather than brand-specific (p. 5). Recipe1M requires sign-up for download (fn. 7, p. 5).
records.ss: word2vec and FastText name matching gave poor results, so string similarity is used (p. 9). USDA categories such as baby food, fast food and sweets were removed to avoid false ingredient links (p. 9).

records.loc: Abstract, p. D950; Materials and methods, pp. D950-D951; Results, p. D952
records.use: Dataset introduction: tabular datasets converted to CSV for Neo4j loading with per-source format files; Ensembl IDs used as external identity links; GO, HGNC, UBERON, BTO, CL and EFO used to unify scientific terms; biweekly backups.
records.dv: GenomicKB (347 million genomic entities, 1.36 billion relations, 3.9 billion entity and relation properties; data and annotations from over 30 consortia and portals, e.g., GENCODE, EPD, dbSuper, RNAcentral, GTEx, GWAS Catalog, DGV, dbVar, 4DN, FIRE, ENCODE, MotifMap, NCBO ontologies)
records.task: Genomic KG construction and integration (schemata, global identifiers, ontologies; tabular sources loaded into Neo4j)
records.ss: different sources describe the same concept differently (e.g., enhancers from ENCODE cCRE and ENdb), which GenomicKB keeps as separate source-tagged nodes (pp. D950, D953).
records.ri: source lists and per-source counts are in Supplementary Tables S1-S2, not in the PDF; no evaluation of integration quality is reported.

records.loc: Sec. 3, Fig. 1, pp. 5-9; Table 1, p. 7; Sec. 4, Tables 2-3, p. 10
records.use: Dataset introduction: source data curated, FAIRified with unique IRIs and aligned to GeoOutageOnto (OutageRecord, NTLImage, OutageMap subontologies); released as Turtle dumps, SPARQL endpoint and linked-data interface.
records.dv: GeoOutageKG (10,965,241 instances, 88,971,709 RDF triples): EAGLE-I county-level outage records for Florida, 2014-2024 at 15-minute intervals (10,635,995 records); NASA Black Marble VNP46A2 nighttime-light images masked to the 67 Florida counties (313,702 images); 15,544 outage maps derived with the VST-GNN ground-truth procedure; GeoOutageOnto ontology
records.task: Multimodal geospatiotemporal KG construction (ontology alignment of time-series records, satellite images and derived maps)
records.dl: EAGLE-I is county-level only, while NTL images are daily only (abstract, p. 1; p. 2). some years have missing days due to gaps in the satellite data (Table 3, p. 10).
records.ss: current content is restricted to Florida (p. 10). meteorological, infrastructure and sociodemographic data are planned additions (p. 15).

records.loc: Dataset, p. 4; Evaluation metrics, pp. 4-5; Table 1, p. 5; Table 2, p. 5 (PDF pages)
records.use: Source corpus and validation: KGs from Graphusion (LLaMA, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o) and baselines (GPT-4o zero-shot, RAG, Local GraphRAG, GraphRAG) rated by two experts on 100 randomly sampled triplets per model (1-3 scale; GPT-4o Graphusion entity 2.92, relation 2.37; without fusion 2.08); Kappa reported.
records.dv: ACL proceedings abstracts 2017-2023 (4,605 valid papers) as source corpus; Graphusion NLP KG
records.task: Zero-shot LLM-based scientific KG construction with global fusion (seed entities, candidate triplet extraction, entity merging, conflict resolution)
records.ss: automatic evaluation is not possible because no ground-truth graph matches the setting, so evaluation is by human rating of samples (p. 4). entities are restricted to NLP concepts; people and organisations are excluded (p. 3). GraphRAG was modified to fit the evaluation, which partly explains its weak result (p. 5).
records.ri: the size of the constructed KG is not reported; the 4,787 documents in the appendix (p. 16) are a separate NLP-Papers corpus (EMNLP, ACL and NAACL 2021-2023, for RAG), not the 4,605 ACL 2017-2023 papers used for KG construction (p. 4).

records.loc: pp. 3-5; Tables 1-2, pp. 4-5; Evaluation, p. 7; Table 4, p. 7; Table 5 and ablation, p. 9; Error analysis, Table 7, pp. 9-10
records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: precision estimated by sampling facts per relation until the 95% Wilson interval width fell below 5%; 22,002 facts judged true or false by four annotators (Fleiss' Kappa 0.505); comparison of genre combinations (Table 4) and pipeline components (Table 5; without document-structure patterns precision falls to 78% and facts to about 80,000); error analysis of 760 incorrect facts.
records.dv: KnowLife KB (542,689 facts, 13 relations, average precision 93%) harvested from a corpus of 1,451,299 documents / 57,235,932 sentences: PubMed Medline 2011 (580,892) and PubMed Central (12,532); Drugs.com, Mayo Clinic, Medline Plus, RxList, Wikipedia Health; Healthboards.com, Patient.co.uk; UMLS as entity dictionary; 467 seed facts from uptodate.com
records.task: Biomedical KB/KG construction from multiple text genres (distantly supervised pattern extraction with consistency reasoning; 13 typed relations)
records.dl: precision varies by relation from 71% (createsRisk) to 97% (sideEffect) (p. 3); preprocessing errors come almost entirely from encyclopedic and social sources (p. 9).
records.ss: recall is not evaluated because no gold standard of comprehensive facts exists (p. 7). no explicit named-entity disambiguation; the most specific UMLS type is chosen and type signatures prune later (p. 5). annotator agreement is moderate (p. 7).

records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: triplets extracted and aligned across sources; KG embeddings (TransE, DistMult, ComplEx, HolE initialised with BERT) generated; statistics compared with other medical KGs (Table 1); 1,000 randomly selected triplets judged by doctors, 94% medically accurate.
records.dv: LMKG (403,784 entities, 1,225,097 relations; 13 entity types, 17 relation types; over 3,000 MB of source text from four medical wikis (A-plus Hospital Wiki, China Medical Information Platform, Xunyiwenyao Medical Wiki, Shiliaotong Food Wiki), the Chinese Medical Journal Network and the Journal of Medical Hepatology, NMPA and State Administration for Market Regulation drug databases, and SNOMED CT; source information retained); RE model trained on CMeIE (CBLUE; over 20,000 documents, about 75,000 triples, 53 relation types)
records.task: Multi-source medical KG construction (NER, relation extraction, hierarchical entity alignment incl. ChatGPT-assisted grouping)
records.dl: relations rest on empirical clinical evidence and lack logical inference such as drug interactions or gene pathogenicity (p. 10).
records.ss: coverage focuses on clinical knowledge with limited pharmacy and biochemistry (p. 10).
records.ri: most sources are Chinese-language web platforms whose content changes over time.

records.loc: Methods, pp. 2-3; Table 1 and Table 2, p. 4; Data Records, pp. 4-5; Technical validation, p. 6; Figs. 2-3, p. 7; Usage notes, p. 8
records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: over 85 million [entity, tag, part-of-text, DOI] records extracted and cleaned; relations weighted by co-occurrence counts; entities matched to Wikidata/DBpedia; annotator disagreement measured per entity type on a random test set (e.g., 2.7% for applications, 22.03% for synthesis methods); SPARQL queries for TiO2, CdTe and graphene illustrate use; released as CSV and RDF.
records.dv: MatKG (over 70,000 entities, 5.4 million unique triples; seven entity types: material, symmetry phase label, synthesis method, descriptor, property, characterisation method, application) built from abstracts of a 5-million-paper materials-science corpus and about 20 million Elsevier figure captions
records.task: Autonomous materials-science KG construction from literature (MatBERT NER, entity cleaning, co-occurrence-based relations, Wikidata/DBpedia linking)
records.dl: MatKG captures connections found in the corpus, not all of materials science; some relations may not hold under scrutiny (pp. 6-7). co-occurrence does not distinguish causative from correlative relations (pp. 6-7). equivalent entities (e.g., CH4 and Methane) are not merged in the current version (p. 3).
records.ss: only abstracts and figure captions are processed (p. 2).

records.use: Dataset introduction: catalogue of properties, units and models forming a directed graph; graph traversal derives further properties from any input set; 'graphical distance' defined as the smallest input set deriving two properties.
records.dv: propnet knowledge graph v2019.07 (115 materials properties, 69 relationship models, serialised in YAML/Python)
records.task: Materials-property KG construction (properties as nodes, physical models as directed edges)
records.ss: the catalogue is a starting set expected to grow through community contributions (p. 465).
records.ri: the graph encodes models chosen by the authors; derived values inherit the approximations of each model.

records.loc: Sec. 2.1, Fig. 1b, pp. 3-4; Sec. 4.1-4.2, p. 14 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction: three-step construction (tool characterisation, schema development, graph population) with iterative refinement through expert validation; also used to generate fine-tuning data for Qwen2.5-7B.
records.dv: SciToolKG (tools from a toolset of over 500 biology, chemistry and materials-science tools; attributes mainly from tool documentation)
records.task: Manual construction of a scientific tool KG (tool and attribute nodes; input/output, dependency, category, source and safety relations)
records.ss: manual construction limits scalability because curating and updating tool information takes effort (p. 13).
records.ri: node and edge counts of SciToolKG are not reported.

records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: LLM pre-annotations validated by four domain experts (Kappa 0.77 for NER, 0.82 for RE); Llama-3.3-70B, Llama-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-V3, ClimateGPT, GPT-4o, NuNER and GLiNER compared with and without PreRAG/PostRAG on relaxed and strict P/R/F1 (best NER F1 0.501 relaxed; taxonomy-guided linking F1 0.367; RE F1 at most 0.078 relaxed / 0.053 strict for Llama-3.3); the reported reduction in hallucination is 23.3%.
records.dv: ClimateIE (new; 25 climate-science publications from Semantic Scholar annotated in INCEpTION: 1,705 entity-publication links, 3,618 expert-validated relationships, 12 entity categories)
records.task: Taxonomy-guided LLM-RAG information extraction for domain KG construction (NER, entity linking to taxonomy, relation extraction)
records.ss: relation extraction remains very weak, and poor entity matching propagates to RE (p. 4302). errors include extracting acronyms without full names and inconsistent handling of term variants (p. 4302). domain-specific validation is needed before claiming effectiveness in other domains (p. 4296).
records.ri: 25 publications is a small benchmark.

records.loc: pp. 1-2; Fig. 1, p. 2; Data availability, p. 4 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction: Sample, Process and Sample-Process nodes with 'Next' edges encoding each sample's experiment provenance; data-file, analysis, collection, Element and pH nodes added; Neo4j database and MPS released.
records.dv: Materials Experiment Knowledge Graph (MEKG; 52,263,968 nodes, 111,430,058 edges) built from the Materials Provenance Store (MPS, ESAMP SQL schema) of high-throughput electrochemistry experiments
records.task: Provenance KG construction for materials experiments (migration of an event-sourced SQL store into a graph database)
records.ri: the graph encodes one laboratory's experiments, so coverage reflects that lab's high-throughput workflows; no quality evaluation of the migrated graph is reported.

records.use: Dataset introduction: biomedical content imported by bots from NCBI Gene, Ensembl, UniProt, InterPro, PDB, PubChem, RxNorm, IUPHAR, NDF-RT, LIPID MAPS, Reactome, WikiPathways, the Human Disease Ontology, Monarch Disease Ontology and others, with structured references; queryable via SPARQL and used for identifier translation.
records.dv: Wikidata biomedical KG (September 2019: over 1.1 million genes and 940,000 proteins from 201 taxa; over 150,000 chemical compounds incl. over 3,500 medications; almost 3,000 human pathways; over 16,000 diseases; 1,502 human genetic variants; Wikidata overall over 750 million statements on 61 million items)
records.task: Biomedical KG integration in a community knowledge base (bot-based imports and synchronisation with source databases)
records.dl: CC0 licensing means datasets and ontologies with more restrictive licences cannot be incorporated (p. 9). community curation can introduce errors and inconsistencies (p. 6).
records.ss: all counts are as of September 2019 (p. 3).

records.loc: Sec. 5, p. 5; Sec. 6, Tables 3-4, pp. 6-7; Table 5 and Sec. 7, pp. 7-8 (PDF pages)
