records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: OSM nodes filtered and typed by the WorldKG ontology; type assertions evaluated on 1,000 entity-class pairs (100 random entities for each of five Wikidata-aligned and five DBpedia-aligned classes), accuracy 97.9% to 100%; entity counts compared with Wikidata and DBpedia (two orders of magnitude more geographic entities); SPARQL endpoint and Zenodo dump; POI query example.
records.dv: WorldKG V1.0 (June 2021; 113,444,975 entities, 828,550,751 triples, 188 countries) built from tagged OpenStreetMap nodes
records.task: Geographic KG construction from volunteered geographic information (OSM nodes to RDF with GeoSPARQL geometries)
records.dl: OSM is volunteered with no strict correctness guarantees; the few wrong types stem from wrongly annotated OSM instances (p. 7).
records.ss: only OSM nodes with tags are used; untagged placeholder nodes for ways and relations are dropped (p. 5). only established tags from the OSM map-feature list are considered (p. 7).

records.loc: Sec. 1, p. 5; Sec. 2, p. 7; Sec. 4, pp. 9-13 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction: domain ontology and nodes created manually; preventive and corrective maintenance activities and image links attached to sub-system nodes; LDT functional groups linked to generic sub-systems; graph released on GitHub.
records.dv: XAI4Wind KG (537 nodes, 1,059 relationships of 9 types, in Neo4j) built from the Skillwind Maintenance Manual and descriptions of the Levenmouth Demonstration Turbine (LDT, 7 MW) SCADA data (102 features, 13 anomaly categories plus normal operation, alarm logs) from ORE Catapult's Platform for Operational Data
records.task: Manual construction of a multimodal O&M KG for wind turbines (sub-systems, SCADA features, alarms, functional groups, maintenance actions, images)
records.dl: LDT SCADA data are confidential, so only publicly available information is included in the released KG (p. 7).
records.ss: the KG is developed manually and is to be expanded as new concepts arise (pp. 5-6).

records.loc: Sec. 4, pp. 20-22; Figs. 2-3, p. 22; Table 4, p. 23
records.use: Validation (dataset introduction): deductive manual coding; encoding consistency checked on eight papers (Kappa mostly 0.6-1); ontology coverage and text encoding coverage computed (average text encoding coverage 84.64%); same papers annotated with FUO and DEO for comparison (PEO ontology coverage 27.78% and 17.52% higher).
records.dv: 40 research papers (2017-2021) randomly selected from the journal Computer Science, manually annotated with PEO in NVivo
records.task: Ontology design and evaluation for academic paper content (PEO: 29 classes, 18 relations, five attributes)
records.ss: figures, tables, formulas, keywords and headings were removed or left unannotated, so text encoding coverage is not statistically accurate (p. 22). after the consistency check, the remaining 32 papers were annotated by the author alone (p. 21). PEO describes only textual content (p. 25).

records.use: Dataset introduction: each entity given a hierarchical path and identifier; definitions generated with Llama-3.3-70B for the 30% of nodes lacking them; taxonomy indexed for RAG and used to validate extracted entities (cosine similarity at least 0.6) before inclusion in ClimatePubKG with provenance.
records.dv: GCMD+ taxonomy (16,360 entities, 18% more than base NASA GCMD; merged from GCMD, CMIP6 controlled vocabularies, obs4MIPs and CMIP Pub Hub; linked to Wikidata); ClimatePubKG assembled in Neo4j
records.task: Domain taxonomy construction as KG schema anchor (taxonomy merging, LLM-generated definitions, Wikidata linking)
records.dl: GCMD+ may not capture emerging climate concepts, and expert-in-the-loop maintenance delays new terminology (p. 4303).
records.ss: predefined relation types may miss nuanced interdisciplinary interactions (p. 4303).
records.ri: the size of ClimatePubKG is not reported.

records.loc: Sec. 3.3 and Sec. 4, Fig. 1, Table 2, pp. 3-4; Sec. 6.2, p. 6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction and validation: OSM keys become classes and key-value pairs subclasses; NCA tag-to-class matches (thresholds 0.25 Wikidata, 0.4 DBpedia) manually verified, giving 100% alignment precision with recall of 63% (Wikidata) and 81% (DBpedia) as reported in earlier work.
records.dv: WorldKG ontology (33 top-level classes, 1,143 subclasses, 1,820 properties; 40 links to Wikidata classes and 21 to DBpedia classes)
records.task: Ontology derivation from a flat tag schema and class alignment to Wikidata and DBpedia (Neural Class Alignment)
records.dl: only 0.7% of about 80,000 OSM keys map to Wikidata classes, limiting alignment coverage (p. 3).
records.ss: recall values are taken from earlier work, not re-measured (p. 6).

records.loc: Sec. 4 'Datasets', Table 1, p. 4; Table 2, p. 6; Table 3, p. 6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: TARGCN (+ DistMult decoder) compared with static KGE, TTransE, TA-DistMult, DE-SimplE, TNTComplEx, TeMP and T-GAP on filtered MRR and Hits@1/3/10; some baseline results taken from Wu et al. (2020), Jung et al. (2021) and Messner et al. (2021). Also used for the analysis of filtered MRR by number of temporal neighbours (Fig. 4).
records.dv: ICEWS14 (72,826 / 8,941 / 8,963 train/valid/test quadruples; 230 relations; 365 timestamps)
records.task: Temporal KG completion (interpolation; time-aware relational graph encoder with temporal neighbouring-graph sampling)
records.dl: timestamped political events of 2014 only (p. 4).
records.ri: Table 1 prints 90,730 entities for ICEWS14, more than the 10,488 printed for the larger ICEWS05-15; the figure equals the total number of ICEWS14 quadruples (74,845 + 8,514 + 7,371 = 90,730; B20-X28 Table I, PDF p. 9), so the entity column appears to hold the quadruple count.

records.loc: Sec. 4 'Datasets', Table 1, p. 4; Table 2, p. 6; Table 3, p. 6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: TARGCN (+ DistMult decoder) compared with static KGE, TTransE, TA-DistMult, DE-SimplE, TNTComplEx, TeMP and T-GAP on filtered MRR and Hits@1/3/10; some baseline results taken from Wu et al. (2020), Jung et al. (2021) and Messner et al. (2021). Also used for the parameter-efficiency comparison with T-GAP and TeMP (Table 3).
records.dv: ICEWS05-15 (386,962 / 46,275 / 46,092 quadruples; 10,488 entities; 251 relations; 4,017 timestamps)
records.task: Temporal KG completion (interpolation; time-aware relational graph encoder with temporal neighbouring-graph sampling)
records.dl: political events spanning 2005-2015 (p. 4).

records.loc: Sec. 4 'Datasets', Table 1, p. 4; Table 2, p. 6; Table 3, p. 6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: TARGCN (+ DistMult decoder) compared with static KGE, TTransE, TA-DistMult, DE-SimplE, TNTComplEx, TeMP and T-GAP on filtered MRR and Hits@1/3/10; some baseline results taken from Wu et al. (2020), Jung et al. (2021) and Messner et al. (2021). Also used for the parameter-efficiency comparison (Table 3); the reported gain over the best prior model exceeds 42% relative.
records.dv: GDELT subset of Trivedi et al. (2017), as used by TeMP (2,735,685 / 341,961 / 341,961 quadruples; 500 entities; 20 relations; 366 timestamps)
records.task: Temporal KG completion (interpolation; time-aware relational graph encoder with temporal neighbouring-graph sampling)
records.dl: facts from 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2016 only (p. 4).
records.ri: few entities and relations with very many facts per timestamp, which the authors link to the large gain from sampling over the whole timeline.

records.loc: Experiments on link prediction, p. 6; Table 3, p. 6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Testing: zero-shot and RAG-based LLM link prediction (LLaMA2-70b, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) compared with supervised baselines on accuracy and F1 per domain; the simplified prompt exceeds supervised baselines by about 3% F1.
records.dv: LectureBankCD (NLP 1,551, CV 871, BIO 234 entity pairs with prerequisite labels; authors' train/test split)
records.task: Prerequisite link prediction between concept pairs (single relation Prerequisite_of; zero-shot LLM and RAG)
records.ri: the RAG data consist predominantly of NLP text, so CV and BIO pairs receive less domain-matched context (p. 6).

records.loc: Drug repurposing, pp. 8-9; Fig. 5, p. 9
records.use: Training and testing: five-fold cross-validation on Wikidata drug indications; performance improved over successive Wikidata versions; external Drug Central test set showed similar improvement.
records.dv: Biomedical subgraph of Wikidata (19 node types, 41 edge types), including historical versions from 2017 and 2018; external test set from Drug Central
records.task: Drug-indication link prediction on a biomedical KG (Rephetio metapath-based logistic regression)
records.ss: gains over time arise from community curation rather than algorithm changes (p. 9).
records.ri: hold-out indications come from the same graph, so cross-validation measures recovery of curated edges.

records.loc: Sec. IV.A, Tables 1-2, p. 4; Tables 3-4, p. 4; Fig. 3, p. 5; Sec. V, Fig. 2, p. 5 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: KG built from authoritative nuclear-power websites and a plant operational-event database; questions generated by a Python script, one question type per triple type; BEm-KGQA accuracy 98.2% vs Bordes et al. (0.908), MCCNN (0.932) and BAMnet; ablations (no fine-tuning, BiLSTM-Attention question encoder, TransE KG embedding); QA system demonstrated.
records.dv: Nuclear power KG (1,298 entities, 22 relations, 2,080 triples; unit information and unusual operating events) and question-answer pair dataset (11,450 / 1,430 / 1,430 train/dev/test) generated from triples
records.task: Domain KGQA with BERT-based KG embeddings (information-retrieval style answer prediction)
records.ss: knowledge in the domain keeps changing; automatic expansion of the KG is future work (p. 6).
records.ri: template-generated questions over a small KG make the task close to relation and entity matching, which may explain the near-ceiling accuracy; source websites are not named and no release is stated.

records.loc: Test dataset, p. 22; p. 23; Fig. 3, p. 10; Table 1, p. 11; pp. 9, 14 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: questions consolidated from external knowledge bases and reviewed by domain experts; accuracy of Llama-2-13b, GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 with prompt-only vs KG-RAG, as bootstrap distributions (150 questions sampled 1,000 times); KG-RAG raised Llama-2 MCQ accuracy from 0.31 to 0.53 (about 71%).
records.dv: Biomedical True/False dataset (311 questions from DisGeNET, MONDO and SemMedDB) and MCQ dataset (306 five-choice questions from the Monarch Initiative and ROBOKOP); SPOKE as retrieval KG
records.task: KG-enhanced LLM question answering (KG-RAG: prompt-aware context from a biomedical KG)
records.dl: SPOKE is built from curated sources but is not asserted to be error-free or ready for clinical use (p. 15).
records.ss: the framework handles only disease-centred questions because only disease concepts are embedded for entity matching (p. 15).
records.ri: per-source question counts and the question templates are in S1 Text, which is not part of the PDF.

records.loc: Methods, p. 3; Fig. 5, p. 5; Table 3, p. 6; Fig. 6, pp. 7-8
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: accuracy of Qwen2-KG (91.67%), Llama3-KG (88.33%) and GLM4-KG (80.67%) vs Qwen2, GLM4, Llama3, GPT-4 (33.33%) and Copilot; answers judged by two domain experts; KG answers inserted before chain-of-thought reasoning in an SO2-adsorbent example.
records.dv: Framework-materials test set (150 questions with reference answers; Table S3); KG-FM as retrieval KG
records.task: KG-enhanced LLM question answering for a materials domain (Cypher retrieval, CoT with KG context)
records.ss: correctness is judged manually (Methods: match with the standard answer, p. 3; Results: two domain experts judging correctness and relevance, p. 6).
records.ri: the questions are built for the KG domain and general LLMs are not given the KG, so the comparison mainly measures access to the KG.

records.loc: Sec. 4.4, Fig. 6, pp. 5-6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Analysis (demonstration): the institution's LLM (URA) generates Cypher over the KG; retrieved triples are verbalised into the prompt; illustrated with a course-withdrawal question.
records.dv: HCMUT educational KG (intent-policy KG in Neo4j)
records.task: KG-augmented LLM question answering (LLM-generated Cypher retrieval of triples)
records.ss: the triple retrieval engine has no ranking mechanism to remove redundant triples (p. 6).
records.ri: no quantitative QA evaluation is reported.
records.dom: Scholarly and education; Legal and public sector

records.loc: Sec. 6.2, pp. 11-13; Table 4, p. 12; Table 5, p. 12
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: questions generated by filling templates from sampled FoodKG subgraphs; KBQA component evaluated with gold topic entities and question types (F1: BAMnet 99.8 / 100.0 / 82.6, overall 95.5; BOW overall 26.0).
records.dv: Synthetic FoodKG Q&A dataset (simple 12,661 and comparison 5,565 questions from USDA data; constraint 6,359 questions from Recipe1M data)
records.task: KBQA over a food KG (template-based synthetic questions; simple, comparison and constraint questions)
records.ss: questions are template-generated with exact entity and relation names, so there is no lexical gap between questions and KG (p. 13). only the KBQA model is evaluated; gold topic entities and question types are assumed (pp. 12-13). no food Q&A dataset on ingredients, nutrients and recipes existed, which motivated the synthetic set (p. 11).

records.loc: TutorQA, pp. 6-7; Table 4, p. 6; Fig. 4, p. 7; Table 5 and Tasks 1-6 results, p. 8 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: pipeline with Graphusion KG vs GPT-4o zero-shot and GPT-4o RAG (accuracy for Tasks 1 and 4, similarity score for Tasks 2-3, hit rate for Task 5, human ratings for Task 6); comparison with CBT, LectureBankCD, FairytaleQA, ChaTa, ExpertQA and SyllabusQA in Table 4.
records.dv: TutorQA (new; 1,200 expert-verified QA pairs in six NLP tasks: relation judgement, prerequisite prediction, path searching, sub-graph completion, clustering, idea generation); Graphusion NLP KG
records.task: Scientific KG question answering in an educational scenario (LLM generates graph queries, retrieved paths used as context)
records.ss: Task 6 answers are open-ended and judged by human assessment (Fig. 4, p. 7). the similarity score is introduced because keyword matching penalises novel but valid entities (p. 7).
records.ri: TutorQA is built around the same NLP domain and KG used by the proposed pipeline.

records.loc: Sec. IV.B, pp. 348-350; Table III, p. 350; question set, pp. 351-352; Tables VI-VIII, pp. 352-354; Fig. 7, p. 356
records.use: Retrieval source, dataset introduction and testing: questions written from the iBKH schema; query-generation exact match 96% / 95% / 86.7% by difficulty; P@5 96.1%, R@5 89.0%, F1@5 91.0%, Hits@k 96.1%, MRR 94.4%; mean latency 6.07 s; case-study queries (e.g., side effects of epilepsy drugs).
records.dv: iBKH representative subset (65,828 entities; 3,004,166 relationships; disease, symptom, drug, pathway vocabularies loaded into Neo4j) and an author-built set of 60 questions (25 simple, 20 medium, 15 complex) with manually prepared gold answers
records.task: KGQA by LLM text-to-Cypher over a biomedical KG (local LLaMA 3 deployment)
records.ss: no prior study evaluates iBKH with the same metric suite, so numbers are not comparable across papers (p. 356). correctness is judged at answer level without semantic-equivalence checks of alternative Cypher queries (p. 356). synonym and identifier normalisation is lacking, which leads to partial answers on multi-hop questions (p. 356).
records.ri: 60 author-written questions; the printed link to the question set points to a generic Google Drive address.
records.met: MRR; Hits@k; F1; Exact match; Runtime/efficiency

records.loc: Sec. 3.1-3.3, Table 1, p. 3; Fig. 2 and efficiency analysis, p. 4; Appendix A, Table 2, p. 7 (PDF pages)
records.use: Testing and retrieval source: multiple-choice accuracy of MKG-Rank vs zero-shot LLaMA 3.1 70B, Qwen 2.5 72B, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Haiku (maximum gain 33.89%); ablation of declarative conversion; caching cuts UMLS query time from 14 s to 0.0009 s.
records.dv: Medical subsets (Clinical Knowledge, Professional Medicine, College Medicine) of JMMLU (Japanese, 450), CMMLU (Chinese, 886), KO MMLU and SW MMLU from Global MMLU (Korean, Swahili; 725 each); UMLS as external KG with a local cache
records.task: KG-enhanced LLM multilingual medical question answering (word-level translation, UMLS retrieval, multi-angle ranking, declarative conversion)
records.dl: Global MMLU contains both carefully translated and machine-translated questions (p. 7).
records.ss: consolidated row (four benchmarks, identical role). content not retrievable from UMLS is handled only by simple BM25 self-knowledge mining (p. 5); incremental databases need a set cloud-retrieval schedule (p. 5). Qwen 2.5 72B drops on CMMLU, attributed to its training data (p. 3).

records.loc: pp. 4, 7-9; Fig. 2, p. 8; Test dataset, p. 22; Cypher-RAG, p. 23 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction, retrieval source and testing: retrieval accuracy 97% for KG-RAG vs 75% for Cypher-RAG; robustness to prompt perturbation; KG-RAG uses 53.9% fewer tokens; context-volume hyperparameter analysis with PubMedBert and MiniLM embeddings (Jaccard similarity).
records.dv: RAG comparison dataset (100 questions built from SPOKE disease-gene associations); SPOKE (more than 40 million nodes, more than 40 integrated biomedical sources)
records.task: KG retrieval for RAG: context retrieval accuracy, robustness and token use (KG-RAG vs Cypher-RAG)
records.ss: Cypher-RAG is sensitive to prompt wording and needs long context windows for complex schemas (p. 23).
records.ri: retrieval questions are generated from the same SPOKE associations that are retrieved, so they test retrieval mechanics rather than open biomedical questions.

records.use: Testing: CNN, BiLSTM and BERT NER models with and without KG guidance; precision, recall and F1 used to compare the KGs; LMKG gives the largest improvement.
records.dv: CCKS19 medical NER (1,000 training and 379 test EMRs, six entity types) and DiaKG (diabetes texts; 22,050 entities, 6,890 relations; nested entities removed); KGs compared: LMKG, EMR KG (647 entities, 3,120 relations) and CSKB (8,722 symptom entities, 146,631 relations)
records.task: KG quality assessment via knowledge-enhanced medical NER (KG features guiding NER models)
records.ss: improvement in a downstream task is used as an indirect measure of KG quality (p. 8). nested DiaKG entities are eliminated for simplicity (p. 8).

records.use: Testing: CNN, BiLSTM and BERT RE models with LMKG entity and relation embeddings (weighted P/R/F1).
records.dv: DiaKG (relation extraction); LMKG graph embeddings
records.task: KG quality assessment via knowledge-enhanced relation extraction (KG embeddings guiding RE models)
records.ss: only LMKG is evaluated, because the other open KGs provide no graph embeddings (p. 8).

records.loc: Crowdsourced curation, pp. 6-7
records.use: Analysis: changes by Wikidata contributors monitored, filtered and prioritised; 2,030 new cross-references to GARD and MeSH added by users, of which 2,007 (98.9%) were judged correct by DO curators and added to the next DO release.
records.dv: Human Disease Ontology items in Wikidata (seeded from late 2015; monthly comparison with DO releases from 2018)
records.task: Crowdsourced ontology curation and synchronisation (Wikidata vs Human Disease Ontology releases)
records.ss: cross-references were added mainly by a small handful of users through one identifier-mapping interface (p. 7).

records.use: Training, validation and testing: resource metadata converted into entity, relation and attribute triples for the KG; CF-KG compared offline with HMM, SAE, FR, BSA, MLP-DNN, DL, RippleNet and KGAT (NDCG 0.625, HR 0.751, Coverage 0.736, CDA 0.741); modality-aware and modality-ablation analyses; CF-only and KG-only ablations.
records.dv: MARS dataset, English-language subset (after filtering: 4,800 users, 14,200 resources (6,200 text, 6,800 video, 1,200 interactive), 132,000 interactions over 14 months; sparsity 0.9981); KG built from resource metadata and transcripts
records.task: KG-supported recommendation: hybrid collaborative filtering and pedagogical KG for multimodal English teaching resources
records.ss: all evaluations use historical interaction logs; the metrics reflect offline recommendation quality, not pedagogical effectiveness or learning gains (abstract, p. 1; p. 7; p. 9). further educational datasets and learner studies left to future work (p. 9).
records.ri: the number of baselines is given as six (abstract), seven (Sec. 3.4) and eight (Sec. 3.2, conclusion); KG size is not reported.

records.use: Analysis (case study): default CKG pipeline reanalyses the clinical and proteomics data; regulated proteins annotated with drugs, diseases, publications and pathways mined from the graph, identifying pathways (e.g., IGF transport and uptake by IGFBPs) overlooked in the earlier analysis.
records.dv: NAFLD plasma proteomics study (ref. 41; healthy/NGT, T2D, NGT with NAFLD, T2D with NAFLD and cirrhosis) analysed against the CKG
records.task: KG-supported clinical proteomics interpretation: biomarker discovery
records.ss: proof-of-concept reanalysis of a published study; no quantitative evaluation of the KG annotations is reported.

records.use: Analysis (case study): of 328 differentially regulated proteins, 188 upregulated; graph mining of drug-target-disease triplets co-mentioned in the literature (3.3 million publications), drug side effects (72,000 associations) and drug similarity used to prioritise candidate treatments and combinations.
records.dv: Urachal carcinoma lung-metastasis proteomics (single patient, ref. 2) analysed against the CKG
records.task: KG-supported clinical proteomics interpretation: drug prioritisation and repurposing
records.ss: single-patient case; prioritised drugs are hypotheses, not validated treatments.
records.ri: literature co-mention is used as evidence for drug-target-disease links.

records.loc: pp. 699-700; Supplementary Fig. 7 and Supplementary Table 5 (not in PDF)
records.use: Analysis (case studies in shared notebooks): CKG reports reproduce published comparisons and annotate regulated proteins with KG context (e.g., COVID-19 severity groups; similarity network fusion for medulloblastoma subgroups; drug exploration for glioblastoma).
records.dv: Brown vs white adipocyte secretome proteomics (ref. 60); longitudinal COVID-19 Olink dataset (ref. 61); medulloblastoma multi-level proteomics (ref. 62); CPTAC glioblastoma discovery study
records.task: KG-supported clinical proteomics interpretation: reanalysis of further studies
records.ss: consolidated row (four reanalyses with the same demonstrative role). the COVID-19 analysis shows the CKG is not limited to MS-based proteomics (p. 700).
records.ri: results are qualitative.

records.use: Analysis: tailored topological indicators (reachability, source indicators, hazard risk via Value and Causality Reachability matrices) computed on the ROAKG to identify key hazards and recommend prevention measures.
records.dv: ROAKG (214 UK railway operational accidents, 2005-2015)
records.task: KG-supported safety analysis: topological analysis of hazard causal paths and risk-based prevention
records.ri: hazard frequencies and probabilities are estimated by counting occurrences across the 214 reports; no external validation of the identified key hazards is reported.
records.dom: Industry, engineering and energy; Geospatial, urban and environment

records.use: Analysis (case study): knowledge base applied to the technological process design of an aero-engine cone gear axis.
records.dv: Machining process knowledge base (KG triples in Neo4j, ontology rules, instance data) built by the framework
records.task: KG-supported process planning (machining knowledge base applied to process design)
records.ss: automatic capacity expansion with machine learning and real-time process reasoning are future work (p. 14).
records.ri: the case study is qualitative.

records.use: Analysis (use cases): SPARQL retrieval of outage records, NTL images and maps for Lee County during Hurricane Ian; described use for multi-hurricane disparity analysis and decision support.
records.dv: GeoOutageKG
records.task: KG-supported power outage analysis (severity evaluation, energy-access disparity, grid operation support)
records.ri: use cases are demonstrated qualitatively; no predictive or quantitative evaluation is reported.

records.use: Dataset construction, training, validation and testing: approved DDIs split 8/1/1 into train/validation/test with an equal number of sampled negatives; KGNN compared with matrix-factorisation, random-walk, KG-embedding and DDI baselines on ACC, AUPR, AUC-ROC and F1 (mean of 5 runs). Also used for the comparison of KGNN aggregation variants.
records.dv: DrugBank V5.1.4 DDIs (2,578 approved drugs, 612,388 interactions) with a Bio2RDF-built DrugBank KG (2,129,712 entities, 72 relation types, 7,852,852 triples)
records.task: KG-supported drug-drug interaction prediction (GNN over drug neighbourhoods in a biomedical KG)
records.ss: DDI edges (ddiinteractor-in) are removed from the KG so that it contains no explicit interaction information (p. 2743).
records.ri: negatives are randomly sampled non-interacting pairs, and pairs are split at random rather than by drug, so performance on unseen drugs is not tested.

records.use: Dataset construction, training, validation and testing: approved DDIs split 8/1/1 into train/validation/test with an equal number of sampled negatives; KGNN compared with matrix-factorisation, random-walk, KG-embedding and DDI baselines on ACC, AUPR, AUC-ROC and F1 (mean of 5 runs). Also used for the hyperparameter study (neighbourhood size, depth, dimension; Fig. 3).
records.dv: KEGG-drug DDIs mapped to DrugBank IDs (1,925 approved drugs, 56,983 interactions) with a Bio2RDF-built KEGG-drug KG (129,910 entities, 167 relation types, 362,870 triples)
records.task: KG-supported drug-drug interaction prediction (GNN over drug neighbourhoods in a biomedical KG)
records.ss: Drug-Drug-Interaction links are excluded from the KG (p. 2743). a separate KG is built per dataset instead of one integrated KG, to avoid losing mutually exclusive information (p. 2742).

records.use: Analysis (application test): LMKG supports medical-record structuring and diagnostic reasoning in a hepatitis B CDSS; 90% accuracy by doctors' evaluation.
records.dv: LMKG; 100 JD Health outpatient records annotated with hepatitis B stages by doctors
records.task: KG-supported clinical decision support (hepatitis B staging)
records.ri: 100 records from one provider; the records are not released.

records.loc: pp. 466-474; Figs. 2-5, pp. 468-473; Fig. 6, p. 475; Fig. 7 and Table 1, pp. 476-477; Experimental procedures, p. 479
records.use: Analysis and validation: propnet applied to Materials Project entries adds on average 29 properties per material (9-fold increase; CdTe example); MIC correlation analysis finds 12 relations above 0.9 (e.g., Debye temperature vs Clarke thermal conductivity, 9 graph units apart); multiple derivation paths give Vickers hardness distributions (GaN vs experiment); five band-gap-to-refractive-index models benchmarked by RMSE against experimental data.
records.dv: Materials Project (over 120,000 computed materials); experimental band gaps and RefractiveIndex.info refractive indices (visible 589.3 nm and infrared) for benchmarking
records.task: KG-supported materials data augmentation, correlation discovery and model benchmarking
records.dl: Materials Project values are mainly first-principles calculations (p. 466).
records.ss: predictions differ considerably from measured refractive indices, especially below about 2.5, and the Ravindra model performs poorly (p. 474). experimental benchmarking data are in the Supplemental Information, not the PDF (p. 479).

records.loc: Sec. 2.2, pp. 4-6; Fig. 2, p. 5; Sec. 4.3, pp. 14-15; Sec. 2.3 (case studies), pp. 6-12 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: questions generated by GPT-4o from tool descriptions, answered via ReAct with GPT-4o, and reviewed by three domain experts; pass rate, tool-planning accuracy (vs expert-verified plans) and final-answer accuracy of SciToolAgent vs ReAct, Reflexion, ChemCrow and CACTUS (n = 5 runs); comparison of foundation models; case studies in protein engineering, chemical reactivity, synthesis and MOF screening.
records.dv: SciToolEval (new; 531 questions: 152 Level-1 single-tool and 379 Level-2 multi-tool); SciToolKG as retrieval source
records.task: KG-supported scientific agent: KG-based retrieval-augmented tool planning and execution
records.ss: ReAct and Reflexion struggle with large candidate tool sets, which the comparison reflects (p. 6).
records.ri: SciToolEval questions and reference answers are generated with the same toolset and an LLM pipeline before expert review, so they favour tasks the toolset can solve.

records.loc: Fig. 1, p. 2; pp. 3-4 (PDF pages)
records.use: Analysis (use cases): graphical exploration of samples containing Al and/or Pd (10,278 samples); queries choosing catalysts for pH 3 OER screening from pH 7 results; evaluation of a catalyst-conditioning (Fe incorporation) hypothesis across electrolyte pH using existing data.
records.dv: MEKG
records.task: KG-supported materials research: interactive exploration, automated design of experiments and hypothesis evaluation
records.ss: the underlying experiments were not designed for the conditioning hypothesis; the evaluation shows it is pH-dependent (p. 4).
records.ri: design of experiments uses a simple correlation rule rather than a learned model, by the authors' choice (p. 3).

records.use: Analysis (proof of concept): BOQA probability for CDDG computed across annotation versions; Wikidata-sourced annotations would have improved diagnosis before their inclusion in HPO.
records.dv: Human Phenotype Ontology annotations (172,760 associations) alone vs combined with 273 Wikidata phenotype-disease associations not in HPO; phenotypes of two suspected CDDG cases from a published case report
records.task: KG-supported phenotype-based disease diagnosis (BOQA ranking)
records.ss: the Wikidata associations came largely from the authors' parallel biocuration on CDDG, so the test is a single-disease proof of concept (p. 8).

records.use: Analysis (use cases): Cypher queries for maintenance actions; PageRank (20 iterations, damping 0.85) ranks sub-systems and fault events; XGBoost + SHAP model of earlier work (accuracy and F1 up to 0.99 reported there) predicts anomalies, and the KG returns preventive and corrective actions (e.g., for a pitch-system anomaly).
records.dv: XAI4Wind KG; LDT SCADA observations (21,392 samples at about 10-minute intervals, 102 features, labelled anomalies)
records.task: KG-supported explainable O&M decision support (Cypher querying, PageRank influence analysis, XGBoost + SHAP anomaly prediction linked to KG maintenance actions)
records.ss: the anomaly-prediction accuracy is taken from the authors' earlier work [42], not re-evaluated here (p. 34). use cases are demonstrated only with LDT data, although the KG is described as not restricted to one turbine (p. 44).
records.ri: no quantitative evaluation of the retrieved maintenance actions is reported.

records.use: Analysis (example queries): genes and variants related to type II diabetes (GWAS, GENCODE, GTEx, GO); positional relation query of CTCF binding at chromatin loop anchors in GM12878 (4,724 distinct loops); agreement between enhancer sources and validation of 16,871 EnhancerAtlas enhancer-gene pairs by GTEx eQTLs.
records.dv: GenomicKB
records.task: Graph pattern query processing over a genomic KG (visual query canvas translated into Cypher)
records.ri: results are illustrative query outputs; query-time or scalability measurements are not reported beyond a stated stress test (p. D951).

records.loc: pp. 2-3; Table 1, p. 3; Fig. 2, p. 3 (PDF pages)
records.use: Testing: execution times of four representative queries (sample, process, provenance and multi-criteria provenance) in the graph database, SQL and file system; scaling of a provenance query with database size.
records.dv: MEKG and the MPS SQL database, with three sub-databases built from the earliest 1/8, 1/4 and 1/2 of Sample-Processes
records.task: KG query processing: graph vs SQL vs file-system queries over experiment provenance
records.ss: the authors do not conclude that graph databases universally outperform other data management methods, only that graph queries are fast enough for real-time exploration and simpler to express (p. 3). SQL query 4 required query-specific optimisation (Table 1 note, p. 3).

records.use: Resource introduction: minutes PDFs processed with a fine-tuned YOLO layout detector and PERO-OCR, NER with XLM-R models via Flair, named entity linking with SPLink, Nameparser, Deep-translator and PolyFuzz; published as RDF with a SPARQL endpoint on LDF.fi and a Zenodo dump.
records.dv: League of Nations Sampo KG / LoN LOD (new; 27 000 pages of LONTAD Assembly minutes 1920-1946, prosopographical KG of about 3100 people; CIDOC-CRM and Bio CRM schema)
records.task: Domain KG construction from archival documents: OCR, NER and entity linking over assembly minutes
records.ss: most false or missing links are attributed to biographical data missing from the external sources, spelling variation (especially East Asian names) and multiple candidates when only a family name is given (p. 10). sustainability of the data service and portal is named as the key practical challenge (p. 17).
records.ri: no accuracy figures are reported for layout detection, OCR, NER or linking. the people count is given as about 3100 (p. 3), over 3000 (p. 5), 3000 (Table 1, p. 7) and 3200 (p. 10).

records.use: Requirements source and mapping target: column-by-column mapping of the four PDH schemas onto OntoPFAS, Schema.org, GEO, DCAT, SOSA and RO terms; example PDH instances released in the repository.
records.dv: PFAS Data Hub (PDH, CNRS Humanities & Social Sciences; about 1M measurements, mainly in Europe, from 143 datasets; four schemas: Known PFAS User (231 users), PFAS Production Facility (20 producers), Presumptive, Measurement)
records.task: Mapping tabular environmental measurement data onto an ontology
records.dl: PDH results from independent assessments that do not share semantics, do not correlate data and have no inference (p. 22).
records.ss: mapping languages are out of scope; the paper shows how information is mapped, not an executed mapping pipeline (p. 31). some columns (pfas_sum, date and year for organisations, internal identifiers) are not represented (pp. 32-33).
records.ri: PDH is described as 143 datasets (p. 22) and as more than 100 datasets (p. 26).

records.use: Resource introduction: Wikidata classes mapped to CACAO concepts (artefact, artist, museum, movement, genre, material), properties restricted to those prescribed by CACAO with original Wikidata URIs kept; dimensions typed and materials linked with Getty AAT; images registered in object storage and a vector database behind an API gateway; snapshot on Zenodo and public SPARQL endpoint.
records.dv: ArtKB KG (new; Wikidata dump filtered to instances of 7848 base classes, aligned with CACAO/CIDOC-CRM/ODRL; more than 8 million triples, 1.4 million entities, 82 classes; about 76K artists, 307K physical artefacts, 2.5K museums, over 4.8K movements, genres and materials, over 147K digital artefacts from Wikimedia Commons)
records.task: Domain KG construction from Wikidata with ontology alignment (cultural heritage)
records.ss: AI-assisted services rely on human-in-the-loop validation, which the authors state does not scale to large collections (pp. 72-73). deployment is a prototype; large-scale deployment is not yet addressed (p. 73).
records.ri: no quality or completeness evaluation of the constructed KG is reported. companion chapter E26-26, citing this KG, describes it as integrating artefacts of three pilot museums (MoMu, Olympic, Aquileia) with Wikidata entities, which is not stated here.

records.use: Testing: CACAO-oriented Text2RDF pipeline (NER, coreference, relation extraction, entity linking, critic agent) evaluated with F1, precision, recall, ontology conformance and hallucination metrics; adding a SHACL tool to the critic raises F1 from .53 to .58, precision from .56 to .62, recall from .53 to .59 and OC from .85 to .90 vs the baseline of the Text2KGBench paper.
records.dv: Text2KGBench
records.task: Text-to-RDF triple generation with multi-agent LLMs and SHACL validation
records.ss: results are described as preliminary (p. 72). generated triples are not ingested automatically and require curator validation (p. 72).
records.ri: the Text2KGBench subset (Wikidata-TekGen or DBpedia-WebNLG) and hallucination values are not reported.

records.use: Resource introduction and validation: GPT-4 with edition-specific prompts segments page-level OCR text (ALTO/METS) into articles, converted with RDFLib to HTO; article extraction checked manually on 100 single-page articles (95% correct) and five multi-page articles per edition (precision 0.88, recall 0.73 over 165 pages); five CQs answered by SPARQL; HTO checked with OOPS (no critical pitfalls).
records.dv: MappingChange KG (new; 10 of 12 NLS-digitised Gazetteers of Scotland editions 1803-1901; 45,651 article-level place descriptions, over 82 million statements, 24,020 concepts, 504,585 annotated places of which 335,249 have modern coordinates; Heritage Textual Ontology)
records.task: Temporal KG construction from OCR'd historical gazetteers with LLM article extraction
records.ss: the 1828 edition (town-focused summary) and the 1848 edition (only Volume II available) are excluded (p. 82). 5% of checked single-page articles contain text from other articles and some multi-page spans are missed (p. 88). evaluation samples are small (100 single-page and 50 multi-page articles) (p. 88).

records.use: Dataset and benchmark introduction: prompts enriched with each item's Wikidata properties (RAG) and sent to Hugging Face models to generate text, image, Braille, speech, music and 3D outputs; outputs deposited per item with DOIs on Dataverse and on Hugging Face.
records.dv: CUBE-MT (new; concept space of 1,300 cultural artefacts in cuisine, art and landmarks from CUBE-1K and the Muse-IT dataset, mapped to Wikidata Q-ids, 18 countries; one benchmark run with 14 models: 10,942 representations in six modalities for 802 Wikidata items (cultural awareness) and 9,600 for cultural diversity)
records.task: Multimodal KG construction with generative models and Wikidata-based retrieval augmentation
records.ss: the model list is replaceable and the published dataset reflects one run with Hugging Face Serverless API models (p. 101).
records.ri: 1,300 artefacts form the concept space but outputs are reported for 802 items. Muse-IT artworks are linked to Wikidata by graph traversal; linking accuracy is not reported.
records.dom: Geospatial, urban and environment; Cultural heritage and humanities

records.loc: Sect. 5, pp. 121-126; Fig. 6 and Table 1, p. 123; Table 2, p. 126
records.use: Resource introduction: blocks of a selected range read from Ethereum (RLP via Web3j) and converted to RDF; ABIs and Solidity source fetched from Etherscan, Solidity parsed to a simplified AST and converted to RDF; user-declared contract licences added; stored in a triple store and on Zenodo (Sancus tool).
records.dv: EthereumKG (new; three interconnected graphs: 2,608 blocks = 8,434,726 triples, 8,283 ABIs = 3,167,373 triples, 94,364 Solidity contracts = 15,555,663 triples; over 27 million triples)
records.task: Domain KG construction from blockchain data integrated with off-chain contract data
records.dl: off-chain ABI and source data depend on a third-party service (Etherscan) (p. 122). most contracts declare no licence (58,317 with none) (Table 2, p. 126).
records.ss: only a selected range of 2,608 blocks is converted; the block range is not stated (pp. 123-124).
records.ri: the KG licence is printed as 'CCA 4.0' (p. 126); no completeness or correctness evaluation of the conversion is reported. the Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.17797524) gives CC BY 4.0 and blocks 17,540,218 to 17,542,825 (web check, 13 Nov 2026).

records.use: Resource introduction and testing: editor JSON exports mapped to RDF with RML (SDM-RDFizer), types inferred from the ontology, and SHACL shapes enforce semantic constraints (e.g., a Train process produces exactly one Model); runtimes for all 61 boxologies: KG generation 2.6 s, SHACL validation 147.0 s, SPARQL querying 0.2 s.
records.dv: Tool4Boxology KG (T4B KG; new; RDF representation of 61 validated boxology diagrams of neuro-symbolic architectures) with the T4B Ontology
records.task: KG generation from architecture diagrams with RML mappings, reasoning and SHACL constraints
records.ss: the ontology is stated to capture only some of the semantics of the diagrams (p. 207). the system does not merge heterogeneous external sources (p. 201).
records.ri: runtime hardware is cut off in the extracted text and runtimes are single aggregate figures.

records.use: Resource introduction and validation: Gemini 2.5 Flash extracts indications, contraindications and adverse reactions; side effects and phenotype terms mapped to HPO by Graph RAG, diseases to MONDO, drugs to RxNorm via RxNav; ShEx validation of all associations and ELK consistency check; 96.5% of 134,515 unique terms mapped; expert check of 980 side-effect mappings from 50 labels: 948 correct (96.7%).
records.dv: SIDEKICK KG (new; from FDA Structured Product Labels, 50,559 labels deduplicated to 18,500 documents; 3,155,094 triples, 205,683 reified clinical associations incl. 184,512 side effects; 6,243 HPO, 2,168 MONDO and 2,370 RxNorm terms; SIO upper ontology)
records.task: Biomedical KG construction from drug labels: LLM extraction and Graph RAG ontology mapping
records.dl: no quantitative adverse-reaction frequencies, unlike SIDER (p. 267). patient-population contraindication terms are hard to normalise (p. 267). relies only on FDA labels, lacking post-marketing, EHR and literature signals for rare adverse events (p. 267).
records.ss: only the OWL 2 EL subset of SIO could be validated with ELK (pp. 263, 267). unmappable side effects are assigned to HP:0000001 (p. 259).
records.ri: SPL source documents are reported as 48,458 (Table 1) although deduplication left 18,500 unique documents (p. 258).

records.use: Dataset introduction: each triple scoped to dereferenceable resources (graphs of 5-50 triples), ssn:Property resources added for lighting data points, and sunlight and occupancy simulated over 24-hour runs on an RDF4J-based read-write Linked Data server.
records.dv: BOLD benchmark dataset (new; built from Brick 1.0.0 'building 3' of IBM Research Dublin from Balaji et al.'s Brick datasets: 24,947 triples partitioned into 3,281 dereferenceable resource IRIs, plus 551 dynamic sensor/actuator resources; 281 rooms, 278 lighting systems; Brick aligned with SOSA/SSN)
records.task: Conversion of a static building KG into a dynamic read-write Linked Data environment
records.dl: the original building 3 graph has no dereferenceable URIs and no temporal entities (p. 328).
records.ss: only lighting systems receive dynamic resources, since all tasks are lighting scenarios (p. 329). the simulation is not claimed to compete with commercial building simulation tools (p. 336).
records.dom: Industry, engineering and energy; Geospatial, urban and environment

records.use: Dataset construction and validation: LangChain chunking, schema-constrained entity types, verb-based relations and Jaro-Winkler entity resolution; extraction accuracy against human annotation of relations between 105 entity pairs from 30 passages (entities 0.901-0.952, relationships 0.871-0.925); graph statistics (degree, centrality, 34 Louvain communities).
records.dv: Rijnmond local news KG (new; Neo4j graph built with GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o or Mistral 7B from 1,200 news reports (894 from the Rijnmond portal plus Rotterdam-filtered national news, July 2022-April 2024) and Wikipedia pages on Rotterdam, 14 other Rijnmond municipalities and 11 local entities; 5,510 nodes with the GPT-4o graph)
records.task: LLM-based KG construction from local news and Wikipedia
records.dl: news data are copyrighted; access only on request to the corresponding author (p. 486).
records.ss: Wikipedia entries for local entities are often missing or sparse (p. 473). the KG is built from static snapshots; dynamic sources are future work (p. 485).
records.ri: the conclusion cites 25 Wikipedia pages (p. 485), whereas Sect. 3.3 lists Rotterdam, 14 other municipalities and 11 entities. the introduction (p. 471) mentions only the 14 municipalities.

records.loc: Sect. 3-4, pp. 24-31; Table 1 and Fig. 4, p. 31; Table 2, p. 34; Sect. 6, pp. 33-35
records.use: Resource introduction and validation: requirements from a chemist and a geographer turned into 30 competency questions answered by validated SPARQL queries; quality assessed with OntoMetrics, OOPS (only minor pitfalls, caused by imports), HermiT consistency check and FOOPS (FAIR score 90/100); usage example for CQ (xi) on PFAS replacement at a location.
records.dv: OntoPFAS (new; OWL ontology of PFAS chemistry, exposure and measurements; 42 classes, 57 object properties, 31 data properties, 207 logical axioms, DL expressivity SRI(D))
records.task: Domain ontology engineering (LOT methodology) with competency-question validation
records.ss: FOOPS score penalised for missing metadata, mainly publisher information (p. 35). the web demo does not yet use the ontology semantics and relies on flat data (p. 35). health and medical aspects are left to extended versions (pp. 34, 36).
records.ri: the repository licence is given as CC-BY-4.0 (p. 25), but reuse is also stated to be subject to a non-commercial licence (p. 26). evaluation is metric- and expert-based; no instance-level KG population is evaluated. the GitHub repository's LICENCE.md is CC BY 4.0 (web check, 13 Nov 2026).

records.use: Source ontologies: soft reuse (selected terms) imported into OntoPFAS for chemical entities, environmental features, exposure agents and outcomes, organismal entities, observations, geospatial data, legislation and provenance.
records.dv: ChEBI, ENVO, EXO, PCO (domain); PROV-O, RO, SOSA, Schema.org, GEO, Allotrope (AFO), DCMI Terms, OCQA, DCAT, SIO, BFO (general purpose)
records.task: Ontology reuse: importing terms from domain and general-purpose ontologies
records.ss: consolidated row (fifteen reused ontologies; family column lists the four domain ontologies). reuse limited to some terms (p. 27).

records.use: Resource introduction: two new ontologies model all properties of Ethereum blocks and Application Binary Interfaces; EthOn is described as outdated for recent Ethereum features.
records.dv: Ethereum Block Ontology and Solidity ABI Ontology (new; extend EthOn and the Solidity ontology)
records.task: Ontology extension for Ethereum blocks and smart-contract interfaces
records.dl: EthOn is stated to be outdated relative to the latest Ethereum elements (p. 116).
records.ri: no ontology evaluation (pitfall scan, CQ testing) is reported.

records.use: Resource introduction, verification and validation: 31 competency questions (14 general, 17 domain-specific) mapped to ontology entities (stated 100% domain coverage); instantiated from DBC files via a KG model (KGM) converted to SQL views, R2RML mappings and Ontop; all CQ test queries executed successfully on the test datasets.
records.dv: DBC ontology (new; extends W3C SSN/SOSA for CAN messages, signals, ECUs, decoding schemas and data logging)
records.task: Sensor-data ontology engineering: CAN bus DBC semantics as an SSN/SOSA extension
records.ss: coverage is assessed against the authors' own CQs; only an excerpt of the CQ mapping is printed (p. 145). an LLM interface for non-expert users is future work (p. 148).
records.ri: no external pitfall or FAIR assessment is reported.

records.use: Resource introduction and validation: structure checked with OOPS (critical and important pitfalls addressed) and FAIRness with FOOPS; more than 20 competency questions executed as SPARQL on KGs populated from industry and research project datasets and from UCR samples; SHACL shapes validate ABox instances; population via a Python library and the LLM-based Code2Onto framework.
records.dv: SemTS ontology with the Data Knowledge and Scenario Knowledge SKOS vocabularies (new; three layers: data management, knowledge classification, knowledge generation; reuses external schemas such as OWL-Time, PROV-O and ML-Schema)
records.task: Ontology and controlled vocabularies for time-series analytics knowledge
records.ss: the CQ evaluation 'confirmed the expected behavior in nearly all cases'; inconsistencies were resolved by updating the ontology (p. 185). an evaluation including reasoning is planned (p. 185). evolving analytical methods and the lack of a standard definition of knowledge challenge the class design (p. 186).
records.ri: the industry and research project datasets are cited but not named or released in the chapter.

records.use: Validation: analysis methods applied to the UCR samples, results instantiated as SemTS knowledge, and competency questions run as SPARQL on the UCR KG with a script provided in the repository.
records.dv: UCR Time Series Archive samples (Trace; GestureMidAirD1) and the resulting SemTS instance KG ('UCR knowledge graph')
records.task: Data-driven ontology validation on public time-series data
records.ri: the size of the UCR KG and per-CQ results are not reported; Table 1 illustrates a single example.

records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: six LLM-based CQ generators (OntoChat, NeOn-GPT, AgOCQs, Pan et al., Rebboud et al., RETROFIT-CQs; GPT-4o, temperature 0, when unspecified) evaluated against the full gold standard with SBERT cosine similarity, BERTScore-F1 and LLM-as-a-judge relevance, clarity and depth; Pan et al. highest cosine (0.32); hit rate per usage scenario.
records.dv: Bench4KE gold standard (new; 843 manually crafted CQs from 17 ontology-driven projects: Polifonia, ArCo, WHOW, HACID, SWO, Stuff, AWO, Dem@Care, OntoDT, Wine Ontology, DOREMUS, NORIA-O, Odeuropa, VGO, VICINITY Core, HCI, RE; inputs are user stories, datasets, ontologies or PDFs)
records.task: Ontology requirements engineering: benchmarking automatic competency question generation
records.dl: the default dataset is imbalanced, input formats are limited to XML, JSON and CSV, and data leakage is a risk (p. 227).
records.ss: several systems were modified to integrate with Bench4KE (pp. 222-223). similarity metrics are approximations; low scores may reflect unsupported scenarios or formats, or fit-but-dissimilar CQs (pp. 224-225). usability feedback came from the authors of three evaluated systems (p. 224). all runs on one laptop (p. 223).

records.use: Target ontologies and reasoning backbone: Graph RAG mapping uses HPO graph neighbourhoods; competency questions use rdfs:subClassOf closure over HPO and MONDO and federated queries over Ubergraph (e.g., 1,903 drugs with cardiovascular side effects; 504 drugs linked to 40 cardiac structures).
records.dv: Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO; over 45,000 terms and synonyms embedded), MONDO Disease Ontology, RxNorm (RxNav API), SIO; Ubergraph for federated axiom queries
records.task: Ontology-based standardisation: mapping clinical terms to biomedical ontologies
records.ss: newly coined or drug-specific terms not represented in HPO caused 10 of 32 mapping errors (p. 264). consolidated row (several target ontologies, identical role).

records.use: Dataset introduction and testing: types and entities sampled from Wikidata with leakage and description filters, statements reduced to five, Prolific annotation with expert adjudication (gold n = 1,080; MCC 0.62); Gemma-3 12B, GPT-OSS-20B, Phi-4 mini, Llama3.1 8B/70B and GPT5-mini (plus multimodal variants) evaluated zero-shot, few-shot and CoT against a no-context baseline; hierarchical macro-F1 about 0.50-0.60 with Delta about 0.1.
records.dv: HERTy-Wiki (new; January 2024 Wikidata dump; 3,776 crowd-verified entities across Art, Building, Location, Organisation and Miscellaneous; 8,767 multiple-choice questions: 6,535 hierarchical (sum; 3,771 most specific, 1,700 less specific, 492 least specific, 572 none correct) and 2,232 sibling; optional multimodal extension with Wikimedia Commons images and OpenStreetMap maps)
records.task: KG entity typing (KGET): selecting the most specific valid Wikidata type with LLMs
records.dl: English only; heuristic filters rely on English labels and descriptions (p. 292).
records.ss: Person and Event domains excluded (p. 282). multiple-choice format is susceptible to selection bias; the no-context baseline cannot fully isolate memorisation; no prompt ablations are included (p. 292). Llama3.1 70B run quantised (p. 288).
records.ri: the text puts sibling macro-F1 between 0.80 and 0.90 (p. 289), while Table 3 reports text-only sibling scores of 0.848 to 0.967.
records.dom: Geospatial, urban and environment; Cultural heritage and humanities

records.use: Resource introduction and refinement: an LLM workflow (e.g., gpt-5-mini) translates framework templates into AgentO RDF; 24 translations (six per framework) reviewed manually, 27 common issues identified and resolved by extending the ontology, extraction re-run; KG published through a SPARQL endpoint.
records.dv: AgentO ontology (new; OWL/RDF; reuses PROV-O, P-Plan and BEAM) and AgentO KG of 66 agentic workflows from AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph and Mastra framework repositories
records.task: Ontology engineering for agentic AI workflows with LLM-based population and refinement
records.ss: only 24 of 66 translations were manually reviewed (p. 307). implementation details (runtime flags, function calls, loops) are deliberately not modelled (Table 1, p. 307). runtime execution traces and alignment with MCP and A2A are future work (p. 312).
records.ri: no quantitative accuracy of the LLM translation is reported.

records.use: Source KGs: person, organisation and place entities of the minutes aligned with seven external services; matched people enriched with name variants, birth and death data, nationalities, occupations, images and LoN sub-organisation memberships; provenance of aggregated triples kept in the KG.
records.dv: Wikidata (1845 people), Lonsea (1686), VIAF (1500), English or French Wikipedia (1289), GND (1187), DODIS (337), Metagrid.ch (314)
records.task: KG enrichment by entity alignment with external authority and prosopographical sources
records.dl: Lonsea site stated to be occasionally unavailable (fn. 12, p. 9).
records.ss: consolidated row (seven sources, identical role). essential data copied into the KG to reduce dependency on primary sources (p. 17).

records.loc: Sect. 4.3, p. 84; Sect. 5.3, p. 89; Table 2, p. 89
records.use: Target KGs and testing: all-mpnet-base-v2 sentence-embedding similarity links articles of the same place across editions and aligns each concept with Wikidata and DBpedia entities; precision/recall/F1 0.79/0.83/0.81 (articles), 0.45/0.56/0.50 (Wikidata), 0.89/0.69/0.78 (DBpedia).
records.dv: MappingChange concept links (24,020 concepts) and external links to Wikidata (7,037) and DBpedia (2,396); manual ground truth of 323 article-to-article links over 175 articles, 114 Wikidata and 71 DBpedia candidate links, 25 place names
records.task: Diachronic record linkage across editions and alignment with external KGs
records.dl: many Wikidata and DBpedia entities have sparse or no descriptions, and Wikidata often has several entities for the same name, raising false positives (p. 89). some gazetteer entries are redirect-only (p. 89).
records.ss: improved external matching via OpenStreetMap is left to future work (p. 92).
records.dom: Cultural heritage and humanities; Geospatial, urban and environment

records.use: Source KG and testing: Stanza extracts LOC, FAC and GPE mentions (precision 0.95, recall 0.83, F1 0.89); Edinburgh Geoparser with GeoNames assigns modern coordinates, 125 of 159 predicted places (78.6%) correctly resolved against GeoNames.
records.dv: GeoNames gazetteer (via Edinburgh Geoparser); 50 manually annotated articles (229 place mentions, 2,275 tokens)
records.task: Toponym recognition and georesolution against a gazetteer KG
records.ss: the annotated sample is restricted to randomly selected articles of at most 200 tokens (p. 89). georesolution prioritises Scottish entries (p. 84).
records.dom: Cultural heritage and humanities; Geospatial, urban and environment

records.use: Benchmark introduction and testing: EnergyBERT embeddings of class names, hierarchies, comments and property domain-range triples produce candidates; DeepSeek gives yes/no equivalence decisions; F1 83.50 (SAREF4BLDG-SARGON), 66.67 (SAREF4BLDG-SBEO) and 41.46 (SARGON-SBEO), above BERTMap, SORBETMatch and AgentOM.
records.dv: SAREF4BLDG, SARGON and SBEO ontologies with manually created reference alignments for three pairs (new; released in the Git repository)
records.task: Ontology matching in the energy domain: encoder candidate generation with LLM binary filtering
records.ss: reference alignments were created manually by the authors; annotation procedure and agreement are not reported (p. 356). no ontology-aware context is given to the LLM, only the two term strings (p. 353).
records.ri: only three ontology pairs; per-pair alignment sizes are not reported.

records.use: Testing: ten configurations (SentenceBERT or EnergyBERT, with or without DeepSeek, single or bidirectional, name/hierarchy/comment evidence); representative Exp5 81.45 P / 45.49 R / 56.33 F1 compared with OAEI systems (e.g., GraphMatcher 78.00 F1, LogMap 68.00).
records.dv: OAEI Conference track
records.task: Out-of-domain ontology matching check
records.dl: sparse and uneven rdfs:comment annotations in the Conference ontologies add noise (p. 355).
records.ss: strict top-1 gate and binary LLM filter trade recall for precision, giving lower F1 than strong traditional systems (p. 355). longer bidirectional prompts made DeepSeek decisions less stable even at temperature 0 (p. 356).
records.ri: baseline scores appear to be taken from prior reports; their source is not stated in the table.

records.use: Dataset construction (SPARQL) and testing: Levenshtein, normalised Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, Beider-Morse and Daitch-Mokotoff scored with a component-wise Dice coverage threshold (best single F2 0.676, NLEV-0.3); Random Forest and XGBoost ensembles with 5-fold CV; LaBSE fine-tuned on the 1,250-pair subset (F2 0.838) and on the full training data (F2 up to 0.912, AUC 0.986); reduced-feature Random Forest (F2 0.740).
records.dv: Wikidata label-alias validation set (new; 9,793 Polish main label-alias pairs of humans with a Polish Biographical Dictionary identifier (P8172) or a 'The Great Genealogy' provenance statement, born 1264-1770; 71,000 negative pairs; balanced training subset of 625 positive and 625 negative pairs)
records.task: Entity reconciliation of historical personal names: string, phonetic, ensemble and Transformer matchers
records.ss: string matching is treated as an early stage; contextual Wikidata properties (birthplace, occupation, education) are deliberately not used (p. 394). no statistical significance testing of differences between ensembles and LaBSE (p. 394). LaBSE needed 45 min 42 s on two RTX A5500 GPUs vs seconds for tree models (p. 392).
records.ri: Wikidata aliases stand in for the CAC-ALMA correspondences that motivate the work; transfer to those records is not measured.

records.use: Source data and deployment: GPT-OSS-120B (on-premise) infers manufacturer normalisation rules (expert-reviewed) and extracts part numbers from QC free text with cross-checks against PLM-DB; an Ontop Lens applies cleaning virtually; direct and by-similarity qualifications retrieved by SPARQL over the VKG, alternative qualifications by vector search (multilingual-e5-large-instruct) and rules, validated by experts.
records.dv: Thales Alenia Space Product Lifecycle Management Database (PLM-DB; tens of thousands of electronic components) and Qualification Catalog (QC; thousands of qualifications), integrated as an Ontop virtual KG (proprietary)
records.task: Semantic data integration of industrial data silos with a virtual KG and LLM-assisted cleaning
records.dl: both databases are manually maintained, with inconsistencies, data-entry errors and key information hidden in free text (p. 401). data and the deployed tool cannot be shared (confidential) (p. 413).
records.ss: in about 2% of qualifications the part number is absent from the description and needs manual handling (p. 405). high initial setup effort (about 60 person-days) (pp. 411, 413).

records.use: Source data: LCA databases accessed through APIs or files and mapped to a unified semantic model with URIs per entity; KBOB data embedded in the KG; GeoNames used for geographical context; access restrictions of licensed databases enforced.
records.dv: ecoinvent (Ecospold), UVEK, KBOB (Swiss building sector) and GeoNames, integrated through the WISER API and WISER KG (ontology inspired by Ecospold and ILCD)
records.task: Harmonisation of heterogeneous life-cycle assessment (LCA) databases through a common ontology and API
records.dl: several LCA databases are paid or licence-restricted (p. 442). Ecospold and ILCD are only partly compatible and need explicit mappings (p. 444).
records.ri: no mapping coverage or correctness figures are reported.
records.dom: Geospatial, urban and environment; Cultural heritage and humanities

records.use: Resource construction and analysis (In-Use): TOVE-based ontology from nine CQs; RML mappings executed with SDM-RDFizer (over seven million triples in under a minute) into product- and month-partitioned graphs with dictionary-based resolution of naming conflicts; seven rules (two materialised with SPARQL CONSTRUCT, e.g., hasNeighbor); SHACL validation; Gephi statistics for one sensor model and month before/after reasoning (edges 16,089 to 18,252).
records.dv: mdevKG (new; Bosch MEMS development KG integrating engineering and manufacturing data; over 3 million nodes and 15 million edges per sensor model per month; SC-Core and specialised ontologies reusing OWL-Time, SOSA and QUDT; proprietary) and a released simulated mock dataset with a simplified ontology
records.task: Cross-domain industrial data integration with a materialised KG, rule-based enrichment and SHACL validation
records.dl: the real KG, models and code cannot be published; only simulated data that do not represent actual MEMS processes are released (pp. 515, 523).
records.ss: implementation scoped to one sensor model over one production month (p. 522). two rules are not expressible in OWL 2 DL and are materialised (p. 514).
records.ri: Table 3's caption cites a reduced network diameter, but diameter is 7 before and after reasoning.

records.use: Testing: mean reasoning time over 20 runs (excluding loading) for inferring all transitive types of :TestVariable with Kolibrie (semi-naive evaluation) vs Apache Jena GenericRuleReasoner and EYE (backward chaining); all systems reported correct results.
records.dv: EYE deep taxonomy benchmark (modified: hierarchy depths 10, 100, 1,000 and 10,000; three superclasses per level)
records.task: Rule-based transitive reasoning over deep class hierarchies
records.ss: a single rule (rdf:type propagation over rdfs:subClassOf) is tested (p. 52). Jena needed -Xmx4G -Xss1G to avoid stack overflow at deep hierarchies (p. 52).

records.use: Testing (results reported from companion work [8]): Mistral-based Text2SPARQL module with entity placeholder resolution against the KB; 100% SPARQL execution success, 79.43% hit rate, 98.43% precision among non-empty results.
records.dv: ArtKB KG with 4,350 synthetic user queries derived from the KB
records.task: Natural-language querying over a KG: LLM-based Text2SPARQL
records.dl: queries are synthetic, derived from the knowledge base (p. 68).
records.ss: figures are reported from [8], not re-run in this paper (p. 68).
records.ri: the 98.43% figure is called precision here, while the companion chapter E26-26 defines it as hit rate among queries with non-empty results (Table 3, p. 498). results duplicate those first reported in companion chapter E26-26 (row B22-R041; Text2SPARQL Table 3, printed p. 498; CLIP results, printed p. 494); cite E26-26 as the primary source and do not count these as independent evaluations.

records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: three experts author seed questions over 40 temporal Wikidata predicates; generalisation by entity/literal substitution, DeepSeek-v3 paraphrasing and pattern-grounded augmentation; answers refreshed against the official Wikidata endpoint; baselines (SF-TQA, EXAQT, LoRA-fine-tuned Llama-3-8B, DirectQA, SPINACH, RTQA) evaluated with answer F1 on a 1,000-question test sample using gold linking; SPINACH best overall (43.9 F1); fine-grained analysis by taxonomy aspect.
records.dv: CR-TKGQA (new; 31,078 questions each paired with an executable Wikidata SPARQL query: 1,076 seed, 12,168 generalised, 17,834 pattern-augmented (sum of the three types) (7,593 SEA, 7,885 TEA, 2,356 ETA); train 21,701 / dev 6,327 / test 3,050 with I.I.D., compositional and zero-shot levels)
records.task: Temporal KGQA with complex reasoning: question-to-SPARQL over Wikidata
records.dl: quality check passed 97 of 100 sampled question-query pairs (p. 162). answers depend on the current state of Wikidata; queries returning empty results were discarded (p. 162).
records.ss: all baselines use gold-standard entity and relation linking (p. 165). baselines evaluated on a random 1,000-question sample of the test set (p. 165). RTQA and the pre-LLM methods are adapted to Wikidata, which may not reflect their original performance (Table 5, p. 165). the taxonomy is categorical and interaction effects between dimensions are not analysed (p. 168).

records.loc: Table 2, p. 158; Table 4 and Sect. 3.2, p. 163; Sect. 4.2, p. 165
records.use: Analysis and testing: TempQA-WD queries parsed and compared with CR-TKGQA on structural and computational complexity aspects and canonicalised query counts (286 vs 10,252); SPINACH, RTQA and DirectQA re-run on TempQA-WD (F1 71.5, 59.5, 52.5).
records.dv: TempQA-WD (SPARQL queries on Wikidata)
records.task: Temporal KGQA benchmark comparison: complexity coverage and baseline transfer
records.ss: 1.3% of TempQA-WD questions combine temporal fact fusion and multi-hop reasoning, vs 33.9% in CR-TKGQA (p. 163).
records.ri: TempQA-WD is described as the only existing TKGQA dataset with Wikidata SPARQL queries, so it is the sole direct comparator (p. 163).

records.use: Testing: nine CQs (e.g., wafers used in a sensor, parts in a wafer neighbourhood, process succession) answered by SQL, manual SPARQL and SPARQL-NLI (each NLI query generated at least three times); answers rated Yes/Partly/No against expert expectations with the implicit knowledge required; query latency for CQ4 (SQL fails on memory; about 4000-6000 ms on the base KG vs 1500-1600 ms after inference).
records.dv: mdevKG variants (base, with reasoning, with reasoning plus SHACL and external ontologies) vs a relational database
records.task: Answering domain competency questions: SQL vs manual SPARQL vs natural-language SPARQL interface
records.ss: ratings are binary or ternary judgements against one domain expert's expected results (p. 516). SPARQL-NLI on the base KG fails several CQs that succeed after reasoning (Table 1, p. 515).
records.ri: the LLM behind SPARQL-NLI and its prompts are not specified in the parts reviewed.

records.use: Source data and training: WIT entity links resolved to Wikidata QNodes, triples filtered by predicate frequency (fewer than 10 mentions dropped) and identifier-pattern removal, verbalised and passed to an LLM to generate conversations, normalised to LLaVA-style chat and filtered by CLIP ViT-B/32 distance (threshold 0.7); SmolVLM and Granite-Vision-3.3 tuned with LoRA (35k/70k, with or without CLIP filtering) and full fine-tuning (70k/140k); training-loss dynamics and qualitative examples reported; pipeline used in Granite-Vision post-training.
records.dv: WIT (Wikipedia-based Image Text; more than 37 million image-text associations) with Wikidata triples of linked QNodes (predicate statistics over about 400k QNodes); generated knowledge-grounded multi-turn conversations (up to 140k samples used for tuning; CLIP-filtered top-35k and top-70k subsets)
records.task: KG-grounded multi-turn visual conversation generation for VLM instruction tuning
records.dl: Wikidata entries are noisy and sparse and false-positive triples still pass the filters (pp. 374-375).
records.ss: frequency-based filtering is a pragmatic heuristic that may amplify popularity bias and drop rare but informative relations (p. 366). reliance on entity-linked pages under-represents visually salient elements not mentioned in the article (p. 375).
records.ri: no release of the generated conversation dataset is stated; only the use of public resources is noted (p. 375).

records.use: Training and testing (results reported from companion work [8]): CLIP ViT-L/14 fine-tuned on the pairs; Recall@1 from 39.36 to 50.97 and Recall@5 from 62.64 to 75.89 over the pretrained model.
records.dv: ArtKB-derived image-text pairs (43,500 pairs from metadata templates plus BLIP captions; 80/10/10 split)
records.task: Cross-modal (text-to-image) retrieval over KG-derived image-text pairs
records.ss: figures are reported from [8], not re-run in this paper (p. 69).
records.ri: textual descriptions are generated from KG metadata templates and BLIP captions, so test texts share the template style of training texts. results duplicate those first reported in companion chapter E26-26 (row B22-R041; Text2SPARQL Table 3, printed p. 498; CLIP results, printed p. 494); cite E26-26 as the primary source and do not count these as independent evaluations.

records.use: Testing and cost analysis: RAG with GPT-OSS-120B (overall F1 0.876; alternative F1 0.619) and Mistral 3 24B (overall F1 0.131) compared against the pipeline output; cost model of person-days for manual, RAG and VKG+LLM approaches over increasing component counts.
records.dv: 675-component PLM-DB subset with qualification matches from the deployed VKG+LLM pipeline as ground truth (17.48% never qualified; on average 0.63 direct, 7.98 by-similarity and 2.23 alternative qualifications per component)
records.task: Qualification retrieval: VKG pipeline vs LLM-based RAG
records.ss: effort figures per component (40, 15, 5 person-minutes) are estimates from a cost model (p. 411).
records.ri: the ground truth is the authors' own pipeline output, so RAG is measured for agreement with it rather than against independent expert labels (p. 409).

records.use: Source KG and deployment: DBpedia Spotlight links entities in titles and abstracts of retrieved results to DBpedia, GPT-4o groups them into facet-value pairs with frequencies; integrated in ORKG (top-15 visible results) and ORKG ASK (top-20 papers by default, adjustable 5-100); runtime about 10.06 s per query over 20 queries.
records.dv: DBpedia (via DBpedia Spotlight) as facet-value knowledge base; Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) content and ORKG ASK corpus (about 77 million articles, 19.1 million with full text)
records.task: Dynamic KG-grounded facet generation for scholarly search
records.dl: DBpedia sometimes suggests general terms not specific to academic research (p. 428).
records.ss: facets are generated only on the visible top results and only on demand (pp. 423, 425). ORKG ASK facets use titles and abstracts only, since full-text access is limited (p. 425). Wikidata and other KBs were considered but not compared experimentally (p. 421).

records.use: Testing: subgraph retrieval around entities of an incoming story, LLM summarisation; context faithfulness (LLaMA-3.1-70B judge validated by a human coder), entity coverage and entity novelty compared with TF-IDF, LaBSE+FAISS and LLM-only baselines (GPT-4o wi+ne coverage 0.793, novelty 0.581; Wilcoxon p < 0.01); four Rijnmond journalists rated 125 background snippets for relevance, serendipity, usefulness and diversity.
records.dv: Rijnmond local news KG (Wikipedia-only vs Wikipedia plus news variants); 45 fictitious news stories for journalist evaluation
records.task: Graph RAG for background-information retrieval in a newsroom
records.ss: no human-annotated ground truth exists, so task-specific metrics were designed (p. 483). provenance links were stored but not shown in the journalist evaluation (p. 478). latency figures (about 400-700 ms) are indicative, not a formal scalability evaluation (p. 484). retrieval and generation are evaluated as a coupled pipeline (p. 485).

records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: CLIP ViT-L/14 fine-tuned with joint contrastive loss (T2I MRR 50.25 to 62.18; T2T MRR 75.22 to 94.73); Mistral-based Text2SPARQL via Sparnatural JSON and SHACL shapes on 4,350 synthetic test queries (100% executable, 80.69% non-empty, 79.43% hit rate, 54.83% exact match); weighted fusion (alpha 0.8, beta 0.2) raises R@1 from 92.07 to 96.37.
records.dv: ArtKB / REEVALUATE cultural heritage KG (cited as [4,5], i.e., the ArtKB endpoint and chapter E26-4; artefacts of three pilot museums (MoMu, Olympic, Aquileia) integrated with Wikidata CH entities; 147,497 artefacts with linked images in deployment, 43,500 at data preparation) and the released image-text pair dataset (new; 43,500 pairs with KG-template and BLIP descriptions and synthetic queries; 80/10/10 split stratified by object type)
records.task: Knowledge-enhanced multimodal retrieval: fine-tuned CLIP fused with LLM-based Text2SPARQL over a cultural heritage KG
records.dl: artefacts often lack values for queried properties (notably depicts), causing Text2SPARQL constraint failures (p. 502).
records.ss: T2T scores are stated to be inflated by lexical overlap between synthetic queries and description texts (p. 495). empty results stem from LLM-hallucinated constraints and BLIP visual features encoded as metadata constraints (p. 498). training and evaluation queries are synthetic owing to data scarcity (p. 502).

records.loc: Sect. 4, pp. 203-205; Listing 1.1, p. 205
records.use: Validation and analysis: diagrams checked against the typed grammar and SHACL constraints (12 syntactically correct, 49 with typing violations that were corrected, 8 with semantic violations); validated models queried with SPARQL for recurring elementary patterns (Listing 1.1; twelve more queries in a notebook).

records.ss: the eight models with semantic violations would require returning to the original papers to correct (p. 204).
records.ri: the abstract speaks of 61 systems from the biomedical literature and 7 from other domains, whereas Sect. 4 describes 69 clinical diagrams of which 61 were validated; the corpus composition should be checked before citing.

records.loc: Sect. 6, pp. 52-53
records.use: Analysis (demonstration): six symbolic rules derive fraud flags, a GradientBoostingClassifier is called through ML.PREDICT on a 14-dimensional feature vector, and fusion rules give a verdict; per-call ML.PREDICT latency of about 138 ms averaged over 60 calls, with a breakdown by component.

records.ss: no cross-engine comparison of ML inference is claimed, since performance depends on the external model and backend (p. 50). scalability is limited by in-memory materialisation of windows, multi-stream join coordination and ML inference cost (p. 54).
records.ri: the origin and size of the transaction data are not stated; no accuracy of the fraud verdicts is reported.

records.use: Analysis: two SPARQL queries (contracts deployed per creator; licences of 'AdminUpgradeabilityProxy'); random walks from wallet nodes and skip-gram embeddings plus Jaccard similarity over 191,146 wallets give 64,201 highly similar pairs and 3,492 multi-address groups; gpuRDF2vec embeddings of ABI semantics cluster contracts and identify identical interfaces.

records.ri: no ground truth is used; findings are qualitative.

records.ss: matched-drug subset only (p. 264).
records.ri: the text gives SIDEKICK's mean similarity difference as 0.1711 (p. 265), but Table 2 lists 0.1711 for OnSIDES and 0.1957 for SIDEKICK. the abstract claims SIDEKICK outperforms SIDER and OnSIDES; only OnSIDES is compared directly, SIDER via OnSIDES's earlier result (p. 264). the text's 14% better separation matches 0.1957 vs 0.1711, so Table 2 is taken as correct.

records.use: Testing: execution times of Traqula's SPARQL 1.1 and 1.2 parsers under several configurations (source tracking, algebra transformation, parser reuse) and against SPARQL.js and SPARQLAlgebra.js; mean AST parsing 2.5 ms vs 23.93 ms and algebra parsing 3.64 ms vs 24.04 ms; recreating the parser per query raises the mean to 689.31 ms.
