records.task: Domain KG construction from multi-source transport data with an urban-traffic ontology
records.dl: traffic-situation data arrive at irregular intervals because of unstable network connections (p. 7).
records.ss: authors state the KG covers only a small scene of urban traffic and plan to add weather and accident data (Sec. 4, p. 19).

records.use: KG introduction: XPath parsing to spreadsheets, imported into Neo4j with py2neo.
records.dv: TCM KG (new): structured pages crawled from vertical TCM websites (A+ medical encyclopedia, Compendium of Materia Medica site); about 7k entities in 9 categories and 7 relationships (TCM and symptom-prescription sub-graphs) in Neo4j
records.task: Domain KG construction from crawled structured web data (traditional Chinese medicine)
records.dl: authors state source data were assessed manually with accuracy above 95% (p. 4267) and that QA quality depends on the quantity and quality of KG knowledge (p. 4270).
records.ri: no evaluation of the KG itself.

records.loc: Sec. III-A-C, pp. 561-562; Sec. III-D, pp. 562-563
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing of a character-based BiLSTM-CRF (F1 'above 97%'), then KG introduction: entities aligned by ssp2vec similarity and fused with structured knowledge-base data via D2R; demonstrated in a web platform.
records.dv: TCM medical-record NER corpus (new): 500 medical records from Chinese medicine books annotated with 13 entity and assertion types under professional guidance (7:2:1 split); TCMKG (new) with an ontology of six classes (disease, syndrome, symptom, therapy, prescription, herb) and five relations; KG size not reported
records.task: Ontology-driven domain KG construction from unstructured medical records with a NER model (TCM)
records.ss: authors plan more corpus to improve NER accuracy and new fusion algorithms to improve KG quality (Sec. IV, p. 564).
records.ri: only an aggregate F1 is given; KG size and fusion quality are not reported; the corpus is not released.

records.loc: Sec. III-B-C, pp. 4-5; Sec. IV-A-C, pp. 6-8 (PDF pages)
records.use: KG introduction: patents manually analysed and summarised into a vocabulary of countermeasure techniques with source references, after unsupervised topic modelling and summarisation proved insufficient.
records.dv: D3FEND KG (new, alpha): defensive techniques and a Digital Artifact Ontology curated from over 500 reviewed U.S. cybersecurity patents (from all U.S. Patent Office filings 2001 to January 2019, vendors from IDC's 2019 taxonomy) and the MITRE Cyber Analytics Repository
records.task: Expert-curated cybersecurity countermeasure KG built from patent analysis (OWL DL)
records.dl: authors describe the patent corpus as partly adversarial, with lower-fidelity citations than academic literature (p. 4).
records.ss: the KG is alpha level and curation was labour-intensive (p. 5).
records.ri: no size statistics or quality evaluation are reported.

records.use: KG introduction and testing of extraction: iFLYTEK Spark with matched few-shot prompts and self-verification reaches NER precision 93.168%, recall 87.772%, F1 90.361%, and relation-verification accuracy 94.0928%; compared with ChatGPT and zero-shot or random few-shot prompting; entities normalised with a TCM terminology thesaurus.
records.dv: TCM KG (new): semi-structured pages from Baidu Baike and Zhongyi Baodian (zhongyibaodian.com) and unstructured text crawled from TCM websites such as Zhongyi Zhongyao Wang (zhzyw.com), accessed 16 April 2023; 8 entity types and 7 relation types; 200 crawled records manually labelled as the test set (new); KG size not reported
records.task: LLM few-shot entity and relation extraction for domain KG construction (TCM, Chinese)
records.ss: authors state that the highly structured dataset made methods score similarly and that accuracy may not reveal differences, calling for more sensitive criteria (p. 17).
records.ri: relation extraction is evaluated as yes/no verification of given entity pairs, which inflates accuracy; raw data available on request only (p. 18).

records.loc: Sec. 3.2-3.3, pp. 5-12; Table 1, p. 8; Table 2, p. 11; Table 5, p. 12; Sec. 4.1, p. 16
records.use: KG introduction: entities (POI, region, business area, category, brand, user, images) and 22 spatial, affiliated, socio-economic and mobility relations; stored in Virtuoso; TuckER embeddings on the Beijing KG analysed for validity.
records.dv: UrbanKG Beijing (1,574,082 entities, 22 relations, 7,535,876 triples) and UrbanKG Shanghai (1,972,385, 22, 9,871,283) (new), from road networks, business areas, POIs (about 1.6M and 2.1M raw records), categories, brands, street-view and satellite images, user trajectories, check-ins, social and attribute data; sample datasets released
records.task: Urban KG construction from multi-source spatio-temporal data (schema, entity identification, relation extraction, attribute enrichment)
records.ri: raw data providers and collection periods are only partly indicated (Baidu Maps cited for online map behaviour, p. 6; WorldPop for population, p. 10); user data come from trajectories and app interaction without a stated consent or anonymisation procedure; only sample datasets are released (p. 12).

records.use: Source KG and KG introduction (demonstration): relationships derived from MAG metadata, stored in TITAN/HBase, served through search, ranking, profiling and visualisation functions.
records.dv: Microsoft Academic Graph (171,233,592 publications, 209,508,429 authors, 196,025 fields; Computer Science subset used); Web of Scholars KG (new): over 1.7 million researchers, 1.5 million papers, 20 million collaboration, 1.4 million teamwork, 1 million advisor-advisee, 14 million citation and 300 million co-citation relationships (over 433 million in total)
records.task: Scholarly KG construction from a bibliographic graph (relationship extraction and profiling)
records.ri: demonstration paper without evaluation; MAG has since been retired, which affects reproducibility; geographic locations come from the Google Maps API.

records.loc: Sec. I, p. 1; Sec. IV-E, Fig. 8, pp. 8-9 (PDF pages)
records.use: Analysis (demonstration): offensive and defensive techniques are linked to digital artifacts, and subsumption over the artifact hierarchy infers which countermeasures relate to which ATT&CK techniques.
records.dv: D3FEND with an OWL DL model of part of MITRE ATT&CK
records.task: Ontology-based mapping between defensive and offensive technique KGs via shared digital artifacts (inference)
records.ss: only a portion of ATT&CK is modelled (p. 1).
records.ri: the inferred mappings are illustrated, not validated against expert mappings.

records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: tail prediction with MRR and Hits@1/3/10 against TransE, RotatE, ConvE, TuckER and FtG; proposed model MRR 0.437 (0%) to 0.342 (40%); ablation at sigma = 20%.
records.dv: Synthetic telecommunications KGs (new) generated from the TM Forum reference model (eTOM, SID, TAM): about 10,000-15,000 nodes and 30,000-45,000 relationships; five variants with noise sigma = 0-40%; 70/15/15 split with 2-3-hop test queries; reference TMF KG released for Neo4j
records.task: Multi-hop path-generating KG completion (seq2seq transformer) on a domain KG with controlled noise
records.dl: authors state real telecom data are confidential and often too small for multi-hop training, motivating synthetic data (p. 6).
records.ss: evaluation on synthetic KGs only.
records.ri: at 0% and 10% noise TuckER (MRR 0.451, 0.418) is level with or above the proposed model (0.437, 0.421) (Table 1); the advantage appears only as authors' injected noise grows.

records.loc: Sec. 3.3, pp. 11-14; Table 10, Table 11, p. 15; Table 12, p. 16; Table 13, p. 17
records.use: Training and testing: TransE, TransH and TransD compared on head and tail prediction; TransD best, head MRR 0.35 and Hits@10 50.0%, tail MRR 0.23 and Hits@10 37.5%; road-speed tail prediction illustrated for the road KG.
records.dv: Public traffic KG link-prediction set (new): 597,216 entities, 4 relationship types; 1,269,031 / 149,299 / 74,647 training/test/validation triples (85/10/5)
records.task: Link prediction (translation embeddings with relation-type-constrained negative sampling) on a traffic KG
records.ss: authors note the KG structure affects the accuracy of the reasoning model (p. 19).
records.ri: with only four relation types the task is close to bipartite record linking; TransH and TransD tie on head Hits@10 (50.0%) although the text says TransD is better on all indicators.

records.loc: Sec. 4.1, p. 5; Table 1, p. 5; Table 2, p. 6; Table 4, p. 7 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: filtered MRR and Hits@1/3/10 against static, interpolation and extrapolation baselines; CENET MRR 51.06 (ICEWS18), 53.35 (ICEWS14), 58.48 (GDELT), with Hits@1 gains up to 8.25%, 8.48% and 20.80%; ablation on ICEWS18.
records.task: Temporal KG reasoning (extrapolation): future event prediction with historical contrastive learning
records.dl: the original ICEWS14 has no validation set (p. 5).
records.ss: consolidated row (three event-based TKGs, identical role).
records.ri: the printed ICEWS14 statistics give more test than training facts, which differs from the usual ICEWS14 extrapolation split; no limitations section.

records.loc: Sec. 4.1-4.4, pp. 5-7; Table 1, p. 5; Table 3, p. 6; Table 4, Fig. 3, p. 7 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: CENET MRR 68.39 (WIKI) and 84.13 (YAGO), improvements up to 23.68% MRR over the best baseline; ablation and hyper-parameter analysis on YAGO.
records.dv: WIKI (12,554 entities, 24 relations; 539,286/67,538/63,110) and YAGO (10,623, 10; 161,540/19,523/20,026), extrapolation versions
records.task: Temporal KG reasoning (extrapolation) on long-lasting facts
records.dl: authors attribute gains to imbalanced recurrence rates in these datasets (p. 6), so results depend on dataset repetition patterns.
records.ss: consolidated row (two public TKGs, identical role).

records.use: KG construction, training and testing (70/10/20 triplet split): link prediction per edge type with AUC, average precision and F1 under increasing class imbalance; AUC 0.82 and AP 0.72; dataset reused from earlier supplier-buyer link prediction studies for comparability.
records.dv: Marklines automotive supply chain KG (built by the authors from Marklines data): 41,986 companies, 74 countries, 5 certifications, 892 products, 35 capabilities; five edge types (supplies to, located in, has certificate, makes product, has capability); test negatives at ratios 1:1 to 1:4
records.task: Multi-relational link prediction (heterogeneous GNN with DistMult decoder) for hidden supply-chain risks
records.dl: data not available for commercial reasons (p. 5610).
records.ss: authors state the model is transductive and cannot reason over companies absent from training, and multi-hop reasoning with unknown intermediates is left open (pp. 5607-5608).

records.use: KG construction, training and testing: same protocol; AUC 0.73 and AP 0.66, lower than the automotive KG.
records.dv: Achilles energy supply chain KG (anonymised oil and gas data, North Sea; built by the authors): 3,967 companies, 61 countries, 3,396 products; three edge types; test negatives at ratios 1:1 to 1:4
records.task: Multi-relational link prediction for hidden supply-chain risks (second sector)
records.dl: smaller than the automotive dataset in size and edge types (p. 5604); not available for commercial reasons (p. 5610).
records.ri: negatives are random non-edges, so missing true links can be counted as negatives.

records.use: Training and testing (analysis): ComplEx, DistMult, RotatE, TransE and TransH in PyKEEN under varied training setups, 100-trial TPE vs random hyperparameter search, repeated model seeds and 10 random splits (10% test); AMR, MRR and Hits@k; RotatE best with the right setup but beatable by TransE under poor choices; DistMult most seed- and split-sensitive.
records.dv: Hetionet v1.0 (47K entities, 2.2M triples, 11 entity and 24 relation types) and BioKG v1.0 (105K entities, 2M triples, 10 entity and 17 relation types)
records.task: Reproducibility and robustness of KG embedding link prediction on biomedical KGs (training setup, HPO, seeds, splits)
records.ss: authors stress that the contribution is not state-of-the-art results but showing that setup, hyperparameters, seeds and splits change model rankings, and recommend reporting them (pp. 1-2, 11).
records.ri: the text states 20 seeds (p. 9) while the Table 6 caption states 10 (p. 10).

records.use: Training and testing: models predict held-out gene-disease links; most perform comparably to the whole-graph setting, ComplEx poorly.
records.dv: Hetionet v1.0 gene-disease edges (10-fold cross-validation, rest of Hetionet in training)
records.task: Gene-disease prioritisation as a domain-specific link prediction split
records.dl: authors note possible trivial examples, since gene-disease pairs linked by upregulates or downregulates can also be linked by associates (p. 10).
records.ss: ComplEx may be sensitive to low data quantity (p. 11).

records.loc: Sec. 4.1.1, Table 1, pp. 5-6; Table 2, p. 6; Sec. 4.2, p. 7; Table 3, p. 8 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training and testing: link prediction (MRR, Hit@1/3/10) against 19 unimodal, multimodal and negative-sampling baselines; AdaMF-MAT MRR 35.14 (DB15K), 35.85 (MKG-W), 38.57 (MKG-Y); ablation on DB15K.
records.dv: DB15K (DBpedia-based with search-engine images; 12,842 entities, 279 relations; 79,222/9,902/9,904), MKG-W (Wikidata subset; 15,000, 169; 34,196/4,276/4,274), MKG-Y (YAGO subset; 15,000, 28; 21,310/2,665/2,663)
records.task: Multimodal KG completion with adaptive modality fusion and modality adversarial training
records.ss: consolidated row (three MMKGC benchmarks, identical role).
records.ri: unimodal KGE and MMRNS results are copied from Xu et al. (2022) while other baselines are reproduced (Table 2 caption, p. 6), so the comparison mixes sources.

records.loc: Sec. 4.3, Fig. 3, p. 7 (PDF pages)
records.use: Testing: MRR of AdaMF, TBKGC and another MMKGC model with and without MAT as the missing ratio increases.
records.dv: DB15K with multimodal information dropped at varied modality-missing ratios
records.task: Multimodal KG completion under missing modalities (robustness)
records.ss: authors state their modality-missing settings are not close enough to real production scenarios (Limitations, p. 9).

records.use: Training: the Shifu2 representation-learning classifier is trained on matched PhDTree pairs and applied to MAG to generate about 1 million advisor-advisee relationships.
records.dv: PhDTree advisor-advisee pairs matched to MAG scholars (ground truth); model applied to all of MAG
records.task: Implicit relation inference: advisor-advisee link classification in a collaboration network
records.ri: no accuracy of the generated advisor-advisee relations is reported in this paper; errors propagate into the KG.

records.loc: Sec. 6, p. 8; Table 5, p. 9
records.use: Training and testing (5-fold cross-validation): document-term features from source sentences classify inference chains; Logistic Regression reaches 92% precision and 96% recall versus 50% precision without pruning.
records.dv: SHKG 3-chain inference set (new; 200 manually labelled inferences, 100 meaningful and 100 meaningless)
records.task: Rule-based chain inference over a KG: pruning meaningless 3-chain inferences
records.ss: 200 labelled chains; chains containing a wrong binary relation were excluded before evaluation (p. 8).
records.ri: labels were produced by the authors; no inter-annotator agreement is reported.

records.use: Testing: Bi-LSTM+CRF entity recognition (precision 0.8234, recall 0.7241, F1 0.771) and Word2Vec template matching map questions to Cypher queries; 81.67% of the 300 questions answered correctly.
records.dv: Hepatitis B TCM KG; 300 manually designed test questions (new)
records.task: Template-based KGQA over a domain KG (Chinese medical questions)
records.ss: authors state the limitation lies in intent analysis: questions outside the manually designed templates receive unrelated answers (p. 7).
records.ri: test questions were written to resemble the templates, so 81.67% likely overstates performance on free user questions; NER training data are not described.

records.loc: Step 3, p. 6; Table 3, Table 4, p. 8
records.use: Testing: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct) given 14 question-Cypher examples generates Cypher over TRisKG; validation set precision, recall and F1 of 1, test set 0.97, 0.94 and 0.95; compared with figures reported by two earlier QA systems.
records.dv: TRisKG; 10 validation questions and 100 test questions formulated with domain experts (new)
records.task: LLM text-to-Cypher KGQA over a domain KG (few-shot prompting)
records.ss: only factoid questions, and only the risk identification step of risk management (p. 9).
records.ri: the 10 validation questions were selected from the training sample questions (p. 8), so the perfect validation score is not a held-out result; comparison with other systems uses their reported numbers on different KGs.

records.use: Testing: zero-shot accuracy of five LLMs (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, DeepSeek-v3, Qwen-Max, Qwen-Plus) with and without KG retrieval; RAG with the KG is reported better on all seven sets.
records.dv: MedKGent KG with MMLU-Med (1,089), MedQA-US (1,273), PubMedQA* (500), BioASQ-Y/N (618) and MedDDx-Basic (483), -Intermediate (1,041), -Expert (245)
records.task: KG-augmented LLM medical multiple-choice QA (retrieval of KG triples as RAG context)
records.ss: consolidated row (seven QA sets, identical role).
records.ri: results are shown as radar plots without a numeric table; MedDDx is described as reducing training-data leakage, the other four sets are older public benchmarks with possible leakage (p. 8).

records.loc: Sec. 4.4-5, pp. 4-5; Table 3, p. 7
records.use: Testing: LLM given the first 6,000 characters of the Turtle serialisation generates SPARQL; 98% accuracy (59/60) versus ChatGPT-4 37% and DeepSeek-R1 52% answering without KG context; per-category accuracy in Table 3.
records.dv: Egyptian COVID-19 RDF KG; 60 fact-based questions (new): 28 factual/statistical, 6 investigative, 6 inferential, 20 general COVID-19
records.task: LLM text-to-SPARQL KGQA grounded in an ontology (GraphRAG-style prompting with the serialised KG)
records.ss: the one error was a fact missing from the KG (p. 7).
records.ri: questions were drawn from the KG's own content and reference SPARQL written by the authors (p. 5), and baselines received no source data, so the comparison measures access to the data rather than hallucination alone; the whole KG fits in 6,000 characters, so scalability is untested.
records.dom: Biomedical and health; Legal and public sector

records.loc: Sec. 5, pp. 6-8; Table 1, p. 7; Tables 2-3, p. 8; App. C, Table 10, p. 14 (PDF pages)
records.use: Testing: Hits@1 of PoG and PoG-E with GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 against IO, CoT, SC, ToG and fine-tuned SOTA; PoG with GPT-4 reaches 81.4 (CWQ), 96.7 (WebQSP), 94.4 (GrailQA), 84.0 (SimpleQuestions), 84.6 (WebQuestions); analyses by entity count, SPARQL path length and graph-size reduction (up to 54% entities pruned on CWQ).
records.dv: CWQ (1,000 questions randomly sampled from test), WebQSP (1,639 test), GrailQA (1,000 ToG samples), SimpleQuestions (1,000 ToG samples), WebQuestions (2,032 test); Freebase as background KG
records.task: LLM reasoning over KG paths for multi-hop, single-hop and open-domain KGQA (multi-entity path exploration and pruning)
records.ss: consolidated row (five QA sets over Freebase, identical role). CWQ test subsampled to 1,000 and GrailQA and SimpleQuestions limited to ToG's 1,000 samples (Table 10, p. 14); ablations on 500-question subsets (p. 7).
records.ri: no limitations section; Freebase is used without discussion of its discontinuation.

records.loc: Sec. 3.4.1, pp. 4-5; Sec. 4.2, Table 6, p. 8
records.use: Training and testing: QA pairs fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B with LoRA; retrieved subgraphs are linearised into the prompt; PlantExpert reaches BLEU-4 57.8%, ROUGE-L 61.6%, Number-Units-Matched 79.5% and human evaluation 82.4%, versus 41.6%, 44.7%, 57.1% and 67.9% for text RAG with the fine-tuned model.
records.dv: PlantExpert agricultural KG; 4,289 QA pairs generated by KG subgraph sampling (new; 8:1:1 split; 428 test samples)
records.task: KG-augmented, LoRA-fine-tuned LLM QA (subgraph linearisation as constraints) with KG-generated training data
records.ss: authors call for large-scale validation on real farmer questions (p. 10).
records.ri: training and test QA pairs are generated from the same KG used for retrieval, which favours the KG-augmented variants; human-evaluation protocol and raters are not detailed in the extracted text.
records.dom: Cultural heritage and humanities; Food and agriculture

records.loc: Sec. V-A-B, p. 69796; Sec. V-D, pp. 69797-69798; Table 6, Table 7, Fig. 8, p. 69798
records.use: Training and testing: XGBoost classifies questions into query patterns from POS and dependency features; entity/class linking by similarity and an MLP predicate classifier fill SPARQL slots; precision 0.86, recall 0.80, F1 0.82 overall, lower for more hops; question classifier 12% more accurate than TeBaQA-feature classifiers.
records.dv: Salzburgerland tourism KG (WordLiftNG project): about 31K facts on touristic entities of Salzburg, 39 properties (10 removed as unnecessary); 700 questions generated semi-automatically from RDF templates of up to 4 hops (new; 75/25 split)
records.task: KGQA over small and medium-scale domain KGs: query-pattern classification with template-generated training questions
records.ss: authors list factoid questions only, exclusion of rare query patterns and false positives from wrong slot permutations (Sec. VI, p. 69799), and state the entity-linking step does not scale to huge KGs such as DBpedia (p. 69798).
records.ri: training and test questions are verbalisations of the same KG templates; no real user questions are evaluated.

records.use: Analysis (demonstration): dictionary-based entity matching and question classification generate Cypher queries; knowledge QA, prescription recommendation and failure cases shown as screenshots.
records.dv: TCM KG (A+ and Materia Medica websites); manually constructed Chinese TCM question set (size not reported)
records.task: Rule-based KGQA and prescription lookup over a domain KG
records.ss: CRF-based recognition was rejected because its speed did not meet QA needs (p. 4268).
records.ri: no quantitative evaluation of answer accuracy is reported.

records.loc: Sec. 3.1, pp. 3-4; Sec. 4, pp. 5-7; Table 1, p. 6; Fig. 2, p. 7 (PDF pages)
records.use: Dataset introduction, training and testing: OpenLLaMA_7b_v2 fine-tuned (QLoRA) on each variant and scored by BLEU, SP-BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L and F1 against reference queries; zero-shot scores about 0; best setting (KQA Pro then Bgee meaningful variables with comments) BLEU 0.588, F1 0.667.
records.dv: Bgee gene expression KG (CC0) with augmented question-to-SPARQL sets (new): five variants (random variables; meaningful variables; original; original with comments; meaningful variables with comments), 513 queries each, generated from about 15 Bgee example queries
records.task: Text-to-SPARQL KGQA over a life-science KG: fine-tuning an open LLM on augmented question-query pairs
records.ss: authors note that augmenting along longer property paths may produce nonsensical question-query pairs needing curation (p. 8).
records.ri: the split between training and evaluation queries is not described, and all variants derive from about 15 seed queries, so overlap between training and evaluation is likely; metrics are string overlap, not execution accuracy.

records.loc: Sec. 3.2, p. 5; Table 1, p. 6 (PDF pages)
records.use: Training: OpenLLaMA fine-tuned for 13,500 steps on KQA Pro before Bgee fine-tuning; helps with meaningful variables and comments, hurts with random variables (e.g., F1 0.392 vs 0.501).
records.dv: KQA Pro (question-to-SPARQL pairs over Wikidata)
records.task: Intermediate fine-tuning for transfer to a domain KG (text-to-SPARQL)
records.ss: authors state Wikidata pre-fine-tuning can make the LLM perform worse than fine-tuning on the domain set alone (p. 8).
records.ri: Bgee was chosen partly because Wikidata contains part of the Bgee data (p. 5), so transfer may reflect content overlap.

records.use: Testing: relevance-prioritized retrieval compared with Langchain-Chatchat RAG and KAG by entity coverage (MDKAG 0.712, KAG 0.702, RAG 0.624) and semantic similarity; answer verification raises the 5-point answer score (domain experts plus QwQ-32B as judge) to 0.751 versus 0.729 (KAG) and 0.693 (RAG).
records.dv: MDKG; question bank generated by an LLM from the 3 x 100 annotated samples (new)
records.task: KG-based retrieval-augmented generation for educational QA (graph retrieval and answer verification)
records.ri: test questions are LLM-generated from the same samples that seed the KG; the abstract's claims of up to 23% lower hallucination and 11% higher accuracy are not traced to a specific table; expert and LLM-judge scores are not reported separately.

records.use: Analysis (case study): Treat relation between tocilizumab and COVID-19 inferred from paths via FGB and TNF using only earlier literature, later corroborated by publications.
records.dv: MedKGent KG (tocilizumab, rheumatoid arthritis and COVID-19 paths)
records.task: Literature-based drug repurposing via multi-hop KG paths (case study)
records.ss: single illustrative case; no systematic evaluation of repurposing predictions.
records.ri: corroboration is anecdotal.

records.use: KG construction and training/testing: KG built from the training folds and used for multi-disease risk classification (5-fold); compared with a rebuilt SHG-Health baseline (Chen et al.) on MAP 0.5019 vs 0.1605, micro-F1 0.4909 vs 0.2160, accuracy 0.8554 vs 0.7158.
records.dv: NHANES (US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey; cycle not stated): 9,770 adult participants (4,626 reporting one or more diseases), 13 self-reported diseases, 318 of 2,585 attributes retained; health KG (new) from Pearson-correlation latent concepts plus expert semantic categories
records.task: Health risk prediction: disease classification of patients over a heterogeneous health KG mined from survey data
records.dl: raw data highly sparse with much missing data (p. 2353).
records.ss: authors state the two semantic relations (containment, related-to) are not distinguished in use (Sec. 7, p. 2360). recall and accuracy differences are not significant (p = 0.056, 0.054; p. 2357).
records.ri: ground truth is self-diagnosis; the fold description contradicts itself (one subset for testing on p. 2353, one subset for training on p. 2355).

records.use: Testing: Naive Bayes diagnosis recommendation over KG probabilities reaches top-5 recall 74.20% and top-10 recall 88.76% against physicians' main diagnoses; KG-based ranking of medicines and exams in a visit reaches NDCG@5 0.87.
records.dv: Southwest Hospital EMR KG; 5,000 held-out visits covering the 500 most frequent diseases; 1,000 inpatient visits for record ranking
records.task: KG-based clinical decision support: diagnosis recommendation and ranking of records within a visit
records.ri: held-out visits come from the same hospital as the KG; the ground truth for record ranking is whether labelled entities occur in the visit, a weak proxy for clinical relevance.

records.loc: Sec. 5.3, Fig. 6, p. 9
records.use: Testing: adding a Bi-LSTM component fed with fixed KG embeddings raises the Jaccard score of disease-to-medicine prediction from 34.7% to 36.4%.
records.dv: MIMIC-III with PrTransH embeddings from the Southwest Hospital EMR KG
records.task: Transfer of KG embeddings to a neural prescription-prediction task
records.ri: how entities of a Chinese single-hospital KG were mapped to MIMIC-III codes is not described; default hyperparameters and a single run.

records.loc: Sec. Methods (KG construction), pp. 2-3; Sec. Experiments, pp. 6-7; Table 1, p. 8; Table 2, p. 10
records.use: Source KG, training and testing: group-aware 5-fold cross-validation with three seeds (15 runs; about 70/10/20 split, zero pair overlap); RA-DDI ACC 0.9234, Macro-F1 0.9102, AUC-ROC 0.9848, AUC-PR 0.9658, compared with DeepDDI, DrugDAGT, KGNN-DDI, SumGNN and others; ablation of seven components.
records.dv: DrugBank release 5.1.13: drug-centred KG with all DDI edges removed (source KG) and three-class DDI relation labels derived from interaction descriptions
records.task: Multi-class DDI prediction with a relation-aware multimodal drug KG (RGCN embeddings, SMILES, BioBERT text)
records.dl: authors state performance depends on the completeness, accuracy and coverage of the KG (p. 11).
records.ss: random group-aware cross-validation does not assess temporal generalisation or cold-start drugs, and there is no prospective validation (p. 11).
records.ri: DDI edges were removed from the KG to prevent leakage (p. 3), a good practice not common in this batch.

records.loc: Sec. Experiments, p. 6; Table 1, p. 8
records.use: Training and testing under the same protocol: RA-DDI ACC 0.8377 and Macro-F1 0.7310 on DDInter; ACC 0.9163 and AUC-PR 0.9844 on PDD-Graph, where KG baselines (KGNN-DDI, SumGNN) are close.
records.dv: DDInter (severity-level annotations) and PDD-Graph (EMR-derived biomedical graph; binary task from patient-level drug co-occurrence with sampled negatives)
records.task: DDI severity classification and EMR co-occurrence DDI prediction (cross-dataset evaluation)
records.dl: PDD-Graph labels come from co-occurrence and may contain noise and indirect associations (p. 8).
records.ss: consolidated row (two datasets, same role).
records.ri: co-occurrence in a patient's medication list is not evidence of interaction; ogbl-ddi is named in the data availability statement but not used in the reported experiments.

records.loc: Sec. 4.2, pp. 17-20; Table 8, Table 9, p. 18
records.use: Testing (use cases): KG embeddings added to task models; mobility prediction Acc@1 0.531 vs 0.442 (ARNN) in Beijing and 0.429 vs 0.379 in Shanghai (7:1:2 split by time); ablations with and without UrbanKG for user profiling and traffic generation; explainable site selection.
records.dv: UrbanKG (Beijing, Shanghai); mobility datasets sampled from user trajectories (Beijing 3,083 users, 12,597 POIs, 650,578 records over 45 days; Shanghai 926 users, 22,627 POIs, 114,811 records over 82 days); base-station entities added for traffic generation
records.task: KG-enhanced urban computing applications: mobility prediction, user profiling, cellular traffic generation, site selection
records.ss: consolidated row (four use cases).
records.ri: only the best baseline is reported for mobility prediction and site selection (p. 17); use cases are demonstrations on the authors' own data without public test sets.

records.loc: Sec. 5.1, p. 30; Sec. 5.4, Table 2, p. 31; Tables 3-4, p. 32
records.use: Testing: zero-shot ACC, AUC and F1 against ConVIRT, CLIP, SLIP and DeCLIP; CMKR ACC 0.501 (COVID-19) and 0.649 (RSNA); ablation shows adding the KG raises COVID-19 ACC from 0.279 to 0.501 at 6% more inference time.
records.dv: COVID-19 Chest X-ray Database (1,200 COVID-19, 1,341 normal, 1,345 viral pneumonia images) and RSNA Pneumonia (5,950 training, 662 test); medical KG named only as "the renowned KG clove garden" (PDF p. 4; no citation, version or size), TransR embeddings
records.task: KG-enhanced zero-shot medical image classification (CLIP with KG explicit knowledge and multimodal-LLM implicit knowledge)
records.ri: the medical KG is named only as "KG clove garden" without a citation, and its construction, version and size are not specified, so the KG component cannot be identified or reproduced; significance is claimed from t-tests with 2 degrees of freedom (p. 31). 'clove garden' is probably a literal translation of Dingxiang Yuan (DXY), a Chinese medical platform with a documented medical KG (SMedBERT, ACL 2021); the paper does not confirm this (reviewer inference(web check, 13 Nov 2026).

records.loc: Sec. 5.1, Fig. 5, p. 30; Sec. 5.3, Table 1, p. 31; Fig. 6, p. 32
records.use: Testing: ACC, AUC and F1 on Atelectasis, Cardiomegaly, Consolidation, Edema and Pleural effusion against the same baselines; hourly diagnosis accuracy of medical specialists with and without CMKR; failure-case analysis.
records.dv: CheXpert (224,316 images from 65,240 patients, 14 observations; five diseases evaluated)
records.task: KG-enhanced medical image classification on a large chest X-ray benchmark and expert-assistance study
records.ss: authors judge CheXpert too large for zero-shot evaluation and use it for general classification (p. 31).
records.ri: the expert study does not report the number of specialists or images.

records.use: Testing: throughput (triples per second) of CQELS+ shared joins vs the public CQELS as the number of concurrent queries grows (Fig. 5).
records.dv: LSBench (printed LS-Bench): queries Q2, Q3, Q5 and Q6, which involve streaming and static data; number of registered duplicated queries increased
records.task: Concurrent RDF stream query processing (shared joins, load balancing)
records.ss: reproduces the LS-Bench experiments with the four queries that involve both streaming and static data (p. 247).

records.use: Testing: end-to-end query latency of CQELS+ under three load-balancing strategies (rotation, minimum average latency, total buffer size) with 1-4 engine instances (Fig. 6), and latency as the number of streams grows (Fig. 7).
records.dv: CityBench sensor streams with queries Q1-Q4 (numerical filters removed); 400 registered queries; number of streams varied (up to more than 30) with Q1 as template
records.task: Concurrent RDF stream query processing (shared joins, load balancing)
records.ss: queries were slightly adjusted (numerical filters removed) so that each sensor observation produces a result (p. 249).

records.loc: Abstract, p. 273; Sec. 4, p. 280; Table 5, p. 285
records.use: Testing: semantic-parsing coverage (97.50% of SIDPs parsed), correctness of derived DL formulae (BLEU of re-generated sentences) and ontology enrichment (798 formulae (85.3%) added; 38 rejected for syntax errors, 9 for inconsistency; Table 5).
records.dv: 960 System Installation Design Principles (SIDPs) provided by Airbus (19.88 tokens per sentence on average, min 5, max 87)
records.task: Mapping natural-language design principles to OWL DL axioms for ontology enrichment
records.dl: the SIDPs are confidential; lexical items in the paper's example were modified (footnote 6, p. 283).

records.use: Source: target ontology enriched with the parsed DL formulae; derived classes matched to existing ones (89 cases) or added as new (935 cases), with consistency and unsatisfiable-class checks (HermiT).
records.dv: Airbus ontology of plane components (about 650 classes, 1,300 individuals, 200 object and data properties, more than 7,400 logical axioms)
records.task: Mapping natural-language design principles to OWL DL axioms for ontology enrichment

records.use: Testing: adapted vs non-adapted importance measures and Relevance by Spearman correlation with query-log class frequency (Fig. 2a), similarity to reference summaries (Fig. 3b), additional nodes introduced (Fig. 2b) and runtime (Fig. 4).
records.dv: DBpedia 3.9 (552 classes, 1,805 properties, more than 3.3M instances) with its endpoint query log (more than 110K queries) as the importance reference
records.task: RDF/S schema summarisation
records.ri: the summary-similarity test compares with "experts' summaries" (p. 398), while Sec. 5 says importance is taken from query logs rather than domain experts (p. 396).
